body: This was an excursion my family and I were really excited about. We were met by our safari driver at our hotel and taken to the park. There are lots of local independent tour operators in the area who are able to do the drives in the park. We had a driver throughout our trip in Sri Lanka and he organised the jeep safari on our behalf. Our jeep driver spoke good English. He encouraged us to stand up as he drove through the park. And it felt exhilarating to drive along dusty tracks, hair whipping in your face, sun shining and excitedly looking out for wildlife. The park had a 'jurassic park' type vive about it........And then we came across monkeys to whet our appetite. Before coming upon a small herd of elephants. There was a female, very, very heavily pregnant- who was likely to give birth in the next week or so. Another female had a baby calf (about 1-2weeks old). The elephants can come VERY close to the jeeps. When there's an elephant siting, a LOT of jeeps descend. And at times, I felt a bit uncomfortable at the number of carfuls of people. However, if the elephants do approach, the jeep drivers do make a hasty retreat. Everywhere you go in Sri Lanka, there is litter everywhere. It was a nice change that there was hardly any plastic waste in the park where the elephants roam.........Apart from one area around the other side of the lake. Tourists are encouraged to get out of the jeep, pose for photos at the waterside, and climb a lookout view point. There was SO MUCH rubbish littered here. As about 100 people were congregated, a shout went out from our driver. A herd of elephants were approaching. Within minutes we were all ushered back into our jeeps. We thought this was for safery, but this was actually so that we could follow them again and watch them enter the water for a refreshing dip. We saw baby elephants, pregnant matriarchs, bull elephants, a few juveniles play-fighting. And we learnt how elephants kick up the grass and loosen it from the ground, pick it up with their trunks and shake out the grass before eating it. They truly are magnificent animals and it was lovely to see them in a natural habitat, where human interaction is limited to about 30-ish jeep-fuls at a time. All in all we saw about 30-ish elephants during our afternoon safari. And a bonus: on our way back to our hotel, we saw elephants in the grass beside the roadside!!
title: Minneriya provides an authentic elephant watching experience

body: On the 3rd day our Exploration of Srilanka, from Anuradhapura to Pollonuruwa, on the way we undertook Wildlife Safari at Minneriya National Park by a private Bollero 4x4 Jeep. From Anuradhapura, it took nearly 01.30 hrs to reach Minneriya National park. We were met by our Jeep Driver who assisted us in procuring our Entrance Tickets costing USD 35 and Jeep cost was USD 40 for a Jeep of 06 pax. Minneriya is a National Park and thereason for declaring the area as protected is to protect the catchment of Minneriya tank and the wildlife of the surrounding area. The tank also is of historical importance, having been built by King Mahasen in third century AD. The park is a dry season feeding ground for large number of Asiatic Elephant population dwelling in forests of Matale, Polonnaruwa, and Trincomalee districts. Minneriya National Park is also famous site for Birding.

body: We have been on many safaris, albeit in Africa, and this is the first time we felt uncomfortable viewing wild animals. The park is small and has limited wildlife (we saw 2 small herds of elephants, a peacock, one empty eagle nest and a wasp nest). On the day of our visit there were upwards of 40 jeeps surrounding a small group of elephants. One of them, "Broken Ear" was known to dislike jeeps due to one killing her baby elephant in the past. Despite this the convoy of jeeps surrounded her, and after two roaring past she became increasingly angry. Our jeep was stuck - due to other jeeps blocking exit paths and despite being one of the furtherest away we were in her line of vision and she charged us, hitting the jeep twice. It was very upsetting to see an animal so distressed and angry, she obviously felt she need to protect her herd which included a baby. It felt so cruel having so many jeeps invading her personal spaceIt is a beautiful area but I really would caution anyone thinking of visiting

body: My wife and I visited the Minneriya National Park in late November 2019 as part of a Webjet package tour of Sri Lanka. The day included a morning visit to Sigiriya’s Lion Rock (which is impressive) followed by a 4wd tour of the park in the afternoon. We were in luck and came across several hundred elephants (guide said 300-400.... maybe) in about 4 or 5 large herds around the edge of the lake. Many babies were seen in different herds. We got within 50m of a few herds as they grazed and moved around the lake edge. Absolutely amazing! Apart from the elephants we saw a lot of bird life and a herd of water buffalo. There were probably 20-30 other 4wd’s sharing the experience so it can get a bit hectic. The elephants generally seemed to ignore the visitors. The only criticism is that our personal guide and the 4wd driver/guide didn’t exactly overwhelm us with information and stayed fairly quiet thru out. Overall a great day!

body: On our trip back from Sigiriya Rock to our hotel, our guide recommended this National Park to go to, We drove here and it was really an amazing and unique experience. We arrived here at the end of the midday at a big parking. This was the departure point for the jeeps. Here we were seated in the back of an 4x4 jeep. First we thought there will be more people in our jeep, but we got our own private tour. Only the 2 of us. haha. The driver drove into the woods, it's about a 15 minutes drive thru the thick woods before you reach the park area. It's really beautiful and breathtaking. The drivers have their route around the park, and off course there were more jeeps driving around. We were lucky that we were late in the midday, so we had only a few jeeps around us. The driver took us around the water and at some point he stops and shutdown the engine so you really can enjoy the beautiful and silence in the park. When your driver sees an animal, he will point at it so you can take a photo of it. In the beginning we saw a group of elephants in the distance and this was really amazing to see in real life (not in a zoo). At some point we drove thru a bushed area and when we reached back in the open again we were surrounded by many elephants and other animals, In 1 word.... WOW!! Really amazing and unique, I recommend everybody who is in the Area or is on Sri Lanka, to go to this National Park.

body: We came to Sigiriya during our roundtrip through Sri Lanka and stayed for two nights at a local homestay. Our plans were to climb Pidurangala Rock for sunrise and for the afternoon of our arrival we had hoped to do a kayaking trip on the nearby river. However, despite mentioned in Lonely Planet's guide, Rasta Rant does not offer those trips anymore.So, we decided to return to our accommodation and since we are quite new to Sri Lanka and it is our first time here, relied on the help of our hosts to arrange the Safari on short-notice, instead of booking an offer we had found on Air BnB. The trip for two people was quickly scheduled and a driver showed up in his jeep an hour later. After driving for a while, he pulled on to a gas station, where he asked us whether we were going to Minneriya or some other park. We quickly said Minneriya, as this was what we had asked for from our hosts.Once we got to the park, the driver (whom we had paid beforehand - 13,000 Rupees for 2 people as agreed with our hosts), went to the ticket counter. While he was gone, a man in what appeared to us as a park ranger uniform approached us and told us that today was a great day to see the elephants. When our driver returned, him and the "ranger" quickly exchanged some words, followed by him also getting into our car, shaking our hands and introducing himself.During the drive he seemed very knowledgable in terms of the different animals and birds, told us he has been working at the park for over 10 years and that he would know all the best spots to see the elephants. Every now and then he hammered against the side of the jeep to make the driver stop and show us something. Everything seemed fine, until at the end of the drive the "ranger" got up to ask us if we were "very happy" and mumbled something about "I really need the tips." That's when we realised that this man is as far away from an official ranger as possible. We passed him some money so he would leave us alone and after again exchanging some words with the jeep driver, disappeared into the woods. We already felt quite embarrassed that we had mistaken him for an official ranger, when our driver made us stop at a local vegetable plantation and encouraged us to buy corn. We kindly refused and were relieved when finally returning to our accommodation. Then, when we got out of the car, he claimed that Minneriya was more expensive than the initial quote and demanded an extra 2000 Rupees from us. We were completely confused, but ended up refusing and walking away from his vehicle.If you're planning on visiting the park - please make sure to compare prices, and don't make our mistake and fall for the false rangers.BUT: The park itself is beautiful, we had lots of close encounters with elephants and other wildlife, saw different kinds of eagles, water buffalos and jackals - which overall, was worth the hassle - so overall - we absolutely recommend visiting the park.
title: Minneriya National Park Safari - Elephants are Beautiful but Tourists beware of SCAMS!

body: we entered the park around 3.30 pm.it was taking 3 hours journey.on the way we saw peacocks , fox , some birds.there a many elephants in the forest.we observed elephants routines & habits , eating , sleeping , bathing etc...we saw 05 baby tuskers.01 tusker called ABHAYA.more than 200 elephants.jeep is good. ( 3500/=)guide also very good knowledge about the elephants who is working @ forest department.05 minutes our guide should fight with elephant by words to while it is coming to attack to our jeep. oh my god what an experience.it is really natural experience how the elephant challenge.took many pictures.guide said deer in the forest & can seen in the morning. & one tiger family also lives.there is one holiday bungalow to stay in the park too.
title: amazing experiance with the elepthant

body: Great place to see wild elephants. Obviously the elephants were enjoying the low tourist arrivals and the menace of safari jeep drivers:-)
title: Lots of elephants!

body: Park with many beautiful elephants that we can see in their natural habitat very closely, in addition to other innumerable animal species.
title: Great Park!

body: Fantastic experience to see so many elephants and youngsters up close. Bumpy jeep tide adds to the enjoyment!
title: Asian elephants and more

body: Minneriya National Park (and the Kaudulla National Park nearby) never fails to amaze me. Easily one of the best places on earth to see elephants roaming in their natural habitat. Seeing hundreds of them in one sighting on any day is guaranteed. Our guide informed that sometimes the numbers could exceed 300. The herds sighted during our visit included several playful young ones who were not allowed by the protective grown ups to stray. it was a wonderful experience. Certainly a must during a visit to Sri Lanka.
title: Many herds of Elephants in the wild

body: A Grate Place to See the Sri Lankaen Jambo (Elephant) in the dry Season (June-September) Big Group of Elephant Gather near the Minneriya Tank with different animals. best to visit evening time.
title: Wonderful Safari

body: We visited the park as part of a tour package and while visits to other parks in other countries have largely been disappointing, this exceeded expectations. I cannot say if we were just lucky but in the space of 2 hours saw close to 200 elephants. They were feeding and walking close to our Jeep. A very surprising and enjoyable experience
title: Elephant safari

body: We went during the wet season so it wasn't super overran with Elephants, but we saw some herds. Overall, a lovely experience but beware: at the start, a tour guide will hop into your vehicle and you might not want that. We didn't and he still came along. We didn't ask him for anything and he was not very knowledgeable about the park. I spotted the monitor lizards before he did and pointed them out to my friend. As a person who is a nature enthusiast, I already knew quite a bit about the animal inhabitants. We also didn't know that the tour guide was coming and didn't bring any money to tip him - only enough to pay and tip our driver. It didn't help that at the end he was asking for a tip and neither of us had the money for him since we did not account for his company. A definite must see.
title: Beautiful experience

body: Nice safari experience. Used to be a good park to see wild elephants. However unfortunately we only could see 3 elephants during our visit. We chose to visit in early morning and some say the evening is the best to see elephants. The views around the lake in the middle of the park are amazing. They stop here for a little while and you can take some awesome pictures here.
title: One of the best parks in Sri Lanka to see wild elephants

body: We had a beautiful afternoon in our private Jeep to Minneriya. We saw well over 40 elephants, water buffalo, monkeys, birds of prey and other exotic birds, deer, lizards, you name it. The guide/ranger was excellent. Do it!
title: Peaceful afternoon with Elephants and more

body: If you wish to observe wild elephants in a beautiful natural lakeside setting, then this elephant reserve is the place to go. It was a wonderful experience. Touring the park in the back of an old 4WD on some pretty rough tracks adds to the excitement and sense of adventure. You are able to get quite close to herds of elephants grazing along the lake side as well as individuals hiding in the thick scrub only metres off the road. Water buffalo herds are also aplenty and were interesting to watch frolicking in the shallow waters of the lake. A storm blew up suddenly while we were out in the parklands requiring the roof of the 4WD to be quickly drawn over us. Then we discovered the mouse living in the rolled up roof and shared the ride with him/her for the rest of the trip. This visit was a truly memorable thing to do and is highly recommended as a must do for anybody whether wildlife enthusiasts or not.
title: Elephants in the wild

body: Sooo we went to Minneriya based on Trip Advisor reviews not the advice of locals. Locals told us the elephants were at Ecopark not Minneriya ( the elephants travel between the two parks). We ignored that advice based on reviews here. At Minneriya we saw 7 elephants in total at a distance. We later heard that most elephants were at Ecopark. The drivers at Minneriya knew the elephants were mostly at ecopark, but need an income so dont tell people this. The next day we went to Ecopark, and saw more than 7 herds of elephants. The elephants do frequent ecopark and Minneriya but check with a local before you go,, to see which park the elephants are currently in. We used ceylon wild trails safari at Ecopark the following day, and were amazed at what we saw
title: Check with locals first

body: This park is stunning. It is all around the most beautiful lake. Our tour guide arranged a jeep for us and he was very good.We saw a couple of female elephants with their babies in the river and then saw a herd of over 20 with very young babies that came by the track right past our vehicle. I was in elephant heaven.A big tip is to go at lunch time. In the mornings the elephants don't tend to come to the lake but as it heats up they come and the park is quiet at lunch time. We arrived there at 12.30 and we only saw 3 other jeeps. We came out at about 2.30 and there was jeep after jeep coming in - they were queuing to get in right back to the car park. We had a job getting out due to all the jeeps. It was manic and awful. We were so glad we were early.
title: So many elephants

body: We saw a herd of elephants (21 individuals) and a few bird species. After that the driver had to drive a one-way loop. To get out of the park at 6 pm he went so fast we didn't see any animals in the forest part of the park. There are 2 loop options. The jeeps have to drive in line, sometimes overtaking each other but there is no way to slow it down and spend more time. Once you are on the loop the distance is so big, the driver has to hurry up.
title: Elefants yes but once you are on one of the 2 loops your driver will just rush you through

body: I had visited the park several times ,this time I do the safari with my Holland friends,I had done morning safaris as well as evening safari,so I found that the evening safari is the best,We saw like 200 wild elephants,freely moving to and fro,very cute baby elephants were there,matured elephants always very much careful about baby elephants,and some tuskers also were there,we did safari at about 3 & 1/2 hrs,our safari jeep was very good,a new jeep,very comfortable,lots of fun with the bumpy roads,we saw deers,monkeys,baffalows,crocadiles,birds,jacoal,folcons,on the way back to the entrance gate, a giant leopard came near by our jeep,we were all silent to see this rarely found animal,our driver told us we were very much lucky to see leopard in this park,this fantastic safari was organized by our driver,complete safari,and very safely we finished it,and very much satisfied about the safari,
title: largest gathering of Elephants in Srilanka,

body: This is a beautiful park. Once you have experienced the jolting ride through the rutted drive way, it opens up into a lake experience with plenty of elephants and water buffalo. Along the way we had to ford a river and one of the jeeps got stuck! Lots of wading birds, egrets, pelicans, cranes, ibis. We also saw a family of monkeys in a tree close up cradling a baby. We also saw eagles in trees. This is a very lively experience. Make sure you are in a jeep with the tarpaulin 'roof' off so that you can stand up.
title: ELEPHANTS GALORE

body: We hired a jeep and driver from Habanera, their company name was Special Safari, the driver was Giayan Kaluarachchi and their number is 0763101482. They are situated in Habanera, near Cinnamon Lodge. We looked on here and took advice to not book in advance, but to go to Habanara and hire a local guide and keep. This was excellent advice. Hire Special Safari as they were fantastic! I read that older jeeps are better as they can go through the water in the park and not get stuck - this was true. We sailed through whilst other newer jeeps became stuck. Our driver was an excellent guide, he knew exactly where to go to see a multitude of animals. We saw: elephants, mongoose, snake, jackals, eagles, deer, herds of water buffaloes, monkeys, peacocks, herons, bee eater, monitor lizards to name but a few. Our driver Giayan was patient, there was never a rush. We set off at at 2.10pm and returned at 6.30pm, giving us 3.5 hours in the park (it's about 30 mins from Special Safari in the middle of Habanara to the middle of the park). We were one of the last jeeps to leave the park as we were having such a great time and our guide was so busy showing us all the animals we could think of!I can't recommend Special Safari highly enough to do the safari in Minneriya. The other thing to note is that the elephants move between parks, so hiring locally meant that Giayan knew exactly where the elephants were and took us straight to them.
title: Wow! Go with @specialsafari01

body: This was good for seeing a high number of elephants together but we had a better safari experience in Uda Walawe. We saw a grey hooded eagle, painted storks, elephants and lots of monkeys here.
title: Good but the elephants were distant...

body: We spent the afternoon here is was the best day seeing the elephants roam free as photography is my hobby the photo opportunities are unreal a must trip
title: Most amazing experience

body: Yes there are a lot of jeeps, but I felt this park was more open and avoided a lot of the crush I felt with Yala National Park (the highlight being to try and spot an elusive Sri Lankan leopard or Sloth Bear). The jeeps on this occasion had room to manoeuvre and the elephants were all very obliging and all jeeps kept their distance and even waited if elephants approached to let them have their way. So I did enjoy this park much more - seeing elephant families doing their own thing without being hassled by the jeeps was most enjoyable. Birdlife was the only other wildlife but there were large and small herds everywhere in this park and I didn't feel the jostling of jeeps too much. Most drove up slowly, found a position and parked to allow us to take photographs or just enjoy their antics. On our safari I didn't feel that the jeep drivers were encroaching on the elephants as all the jeeps seem to follow the track, parked off to the side and allowed us to just watch the elephants - yes mothers put their babies on the other side of the jeeps, but continued feeding, and the babies of course continued playing.I actually quite enjoyed the afternoon safari as instead of getting hotter, it cooled as the afternoon sun began to set. We were a private group with our own guide so we had a pre-arranged driver for this attraction, so it was just us in a slightly newer and more comfortable jeep - open topped and a little dusty, but allowed you to stand and take photos when the jeep stopped.Have an open mind here - Sri Lankan is a developing country and has a long way to go so don't expect the same level of eco-tourism you would get in other countries.
title: Enjoyable afternoon jeep ride

body: We felt something wrong going on when we reached to the location between our taxi driver and the jeep driver ,Then we figured out that they were manipulate. The jeep driver was asking for double amount.He asked for 220 USD for the couple included the car while the actual price should be around 100 USD Only or even less.Therefore,You have to make sure to get the ticket by yourself OR to receive the receipt of paid amount.In addition to the above, we read that the safari should take about 3 hours to 3 and half while our tour was less about an hour only after the above incident, we haven’t seen anything just two elephants!!
title: Bad experience !!!!!

body: A great safari with a lot of elephants and water buffaloes which we saw from a very short distance. On top of the tickets you pay 7000 LKR for a jeep. We had a good luck and saw dozens of elephants and even more water buffaloes. There were more jeeps than I would prefer, which makes it too busy, but it was still an amazing experience.
title: Don’t miss it

body: This is a good place to see elephants in the wild. Depending on your luck you may see 20 or more elephants in groups. It is a busy place. Lots of jeeps. Just make sure to be careful of low hanging branches and narrow passages through thick vegetation, especially on the way back once the safari is over. We saw one of the visitors got a cut on face after getting hit by a tree branch on the way back from safari. And it is an open top safari. So apply plenty of sun screen and wear good sun protection. Also it can be dusty and so bring a mask if you have dust allergies.
title: Elephant safari

body: This is the perfect drive in the evening, even though we didn't have any plan of visiting this park, our guide suggested to do this, so we went ahead and we were not disappointed. It's an 2-3 hour long Safari in the park and they take you near the lake where elephants come there to eat. It's the perfect time to visit as you would end up seeing so many so close. I think they are used to so many jeeps coming close everyday so they were busy eating and we were ignored most of the time by them. So we closely watched how they eat the grass, the way they pull out, dust it out and then eat. It was an amazing experience to watch them so close. We were taken another side of the lake for a nice view which you can climb few stairs to watch and if you are keen just to get the legs dirty after. The surprising visitors were variety of birds, they were awesome. I wish I had more time to spot them more.
title: Evening drive

body: Went at about 1:30pm; yes it was hot! But it was outstanding plenty of elephants, Monkeys, Deer, water buffalo, monitor lizards, Turtles and plenty of beautiful birds. Going on the earlier tour there were only a maximum of 5 Jeeps at once stopped looking at the elephants and felt like we saw the animals in their natural habitat and when we were leaving the park at around 3:30 there must have been around 50 odd Jeeps lining up to see a heard of elephants in which we saw earlier and plenty more entering the park as we left. Was a truly wonderful experience!
title: Bet the rush to see the elephants!

body: Were not sure how good this was going to be when we saw the number of vehicles heading into the park. Initially saw a couple but then as se went around the lakeside there were 40/50 elephants quietly grazing. Although there are lots of vehicles they seem to stick to the tracks and everyone has got the opportunity to see the elephants and get some good photos. Very enjoyable.
title: Afternoon drive

body: We went on a morning safari and made it to the elephant herd just before they went into the jungle. It was nice, but I think you'll have more chances to see them on a night safari when they come to the lake to drink. The park itself is amazingly beautiful. Safaris don't provide you with anything and you have to pay the entrance fee yourself so bring water and money. Expect to pay around 4000 LKR for 2 people. It's worth your time and money.
title: Take the evening safari

body: Amazing gathering of over 200 elephants...including playful calves suckling their mothers! Best to go in the evening around 5pm...as they come towards the Minneriya Tank built by one of the ancient Kings of Sri Lanka. King Mahasen also known as "The god of Minneriya" or "Minneriya deviyo" His statue is on the roundabout at Habarana.100s of vehicles also arrive to wstch the elephants but they don't seem to be bothered by this.It can be very dusty so it's best to tie a scarf over your hair and perhaps over your face too!
title: Elephant Gathering Minneriya

body: We had a wonderful experience at Mineriya National Park. We saw more than 70 elephants in groups playing and interacting with each other. It is something that everyone should experience. I will certainly go there again.
title: Great safari experience

body: If you are looking for an exclusive observation of elephants grazing in herds by the lake edge you are going to be disappointed. This is a popular tourist attraction and the convoy of vehicles winding their way along the dirt roads to find elephants is at times intrusive. Having said that you are likely to have the opportunity to see groups of elephants as we did. There were many with young, one or two month old babies and they genuinely seemed unconcerned with the vehicles nearby. For the most part drivers showed some respect for the elephant’s welfare and maintained a good distance. In many instances the elephants ambled slowly closer to the vehicles. If you decide to go my suggestion would be to go late afternoon, say from 3.00pm onwards. This way you escape the heat of the day. There are dozens of drivers outside the park entrance ready to take you.
title: Not for the purist

body: We went to Minneriya national park and booked a Private Jeep and driver recommended by one of our Colombo friend his name is jayalath and can be contacted on 0771278352. He charged us 3500 srilankan rupees . Usually hotel charge 5000 . So it’s was a good deal driver was very informative and explained us about most of the animals . As it was too early in morning so was little difficult to see elephants but he did his best to show us and finally we saw a few , it tools around 3 hours altogether and the entry fees was seperate which was around 8000 srilanka rupees for two foreigners two locals and taxes included . So basically we paid $100 au dollars all together including Jeep hiring. But it was soo beautiful and lovely to see wild animals without any animal cruelty. Worth every cent. Thankyou jayalath .
title: Nice place

body: Had a half day visit to Minneriya. Highlight was around 30-40 elephants emerging from forest to 'take the waters'. An awful lot of trucks vying for best position, but got a good long view of several heards around the park. Lots of birdlife and buffalo also. A 'must see'.
title: Wonderful heard of elephants.

body: I did a lot of research before taking this safari and was a little concerned about if the animals would be treated respectfull. As it turned out I was pleasantly surprised. Yes, there are a lot of jeeps but they all stay on the tracks and don't speed or chase the elephants. We went in the afternoon and saw loads of elephants and babies too. As well as that we saw buffalo, deer, langurs and many birds including sea eagles. As an animal lover this was a highlight of my trip to Sri Lanka.
title: Wonderful elephants

body: Minneriya National Park was an incredible place and experience. The park is beautiful and we saw hundreds of elephants on our loop through the park. The drivers were careful and respectful of the animals.
title: Highlight on our trip!

body: This was our first (of 3) safari experiences in Sri Lanka. The jeep was in average condition, 3 rows of seats, with open roofs where you could stand up. All the jeeps follow the same track, up to 2 abreast at a time. You go through bush, then through a river (3 jeeps got stuck - fortunately not ours) and then it opens out to large areas surrounding the lake. We saw a couple of hundred elephants (best to go on an afternoon safari as they come to the lake for water). Unfortunately there were almost as many jeeps as elephants and at first we sat in a huge queue (the jeeps at the front of the line didn't move on in a timely manner). After a while the jeeps spread out and there were plenty more elephants to see, with less crowded jeep conditions. Our driver didn't really talk to us, but it was pretty obvious what we were looking at! If you're into elephants this is the safari for you.
title: Elephants galore!

body: Make sure that you pick the right guide. Some clearly just roar around as fast as possible in unsuitable vehicles. Others are great and gives you a detailed view of what's going on and get you really close.
title: Pick right!

body: We were left slightly underwhelmed. The park was very busy and there was a lot of jostling to get into positions. The variety of animals was disappointing, and every bird of prey was an eagle...... the elephants are in abundance and very docile so you get up close to them.
title: Visit to Park

body: Great way to see elephants and lots of bird life. The driver was great, making sure we had seen enough before moving on again. Highly recommended
title: Excellent safari we saw so many elephants

body: Sadly this wildlife park is being over-exploited, with convoys of jeeps in search of a limited number of elephants. When a herd was spotted, the dirt track turned into a 4x4 sales forecourt, with jeeps jostling for space and the best view.We also saw a few larger birds (egrets, eagles, herons and pelicans), and a mongoose. Ironically, we saw two elephants (one of them with tasks, quite rare) by the side of the road on our drive back to the hotel. Our driver was quick to spot them in the semi-darkness, and we were much closer to them than in the wildlife park.Our expectations may have been too high, as we had already visited Yala National Park earlier in our holiday. I would give Minneriya a miss and spend the extra time at Yala. A more diverse range of animals and birds, with less jeeps!!
title: Too many jeeps

body: Great park , you see Elephant really clearly. On my visit there was a herd with a 3 week old calf who was feeding. In another area another herd with a young calf who was trumpetting, I also saw Giant Squirrel and 6 times The Jungle Fowl Sri Lankas national bird. My driver arranged an earlier visit than planned to avoid the many jeeps on our way out there were many many jeeps. So if your goings get some good advice and go a little earlier.
title: Amazing to see Elephant

body: Loved this adventure. Our safari had a fun start with one jeep bogged in the river. Then there was great excitement when we spotted our first wild elephant, then another and another. Then there were dozens of them gathering near the lake, one only a month old. Very special indeed.
title: Elephants, elephants, elephants.

body: I had no high expectations prior to our jeep safari but maybe by luck or chance we had a great experience. We did see a lot of elephants but more significantly was the fact that we saw them in herds of at least 40-50 with babies! The park is very open so we were able to get quite close, many photo opportunities. Also saw an abundance of bird life, water buffaloes, monitors etc. The safaris seem to take about 2 hours. Wear sunscreen as the jeeps are open top and plan to have a good long shower back at your accommodation to wash of all the dust! Great experience.
title: It's All About The Elephants

body: You can club this safari along your visit to the sigiriya rock. Your car will take you to the place from where the safari begins. You will sit in jeeps and trek into the jungles. The jungle is dark and at times the ride gets too bumpy. After a good 30-45 mins one lane trekking you will get onto a plain where you can see herd of elephants in wild. Its a cute sight. We also spotted peacocks, a wild bull who ran past our jeeps (completely safe) and a few birds of different species. We stayed there for another 30 mins. The elephants seemed human friendly. They were very near to our jeeps but they were of no harm to us. Getting out of the jeep is strictly prohibited. Pregnant ladies do not take this ride even if its your first trimester. I had my two kids with me. They loved and enjoyed the bumpy ride more than the elephants watching. Overall its a good experience but nothing exceptional about it.
title: Nice

body: Well worth going if you want to see elephants. I was happy if we saw 3 or 4, but we ended up seeing hundreds. At times elephants in every direction we looked.First 30 to 40 mins through dense jungle so you are unlikely to see anything, but then scenery opens up and in open grassland with herds of elephants. When we thought we had seen then all turned another corner and there were more.Also saw water Buffulo, a jacket and lots of birds including egrets, cranes,storks, peacocks and eagles
title: Elephants everywhere

body: Beginning the tour we were apprehensive as to whether we would be fortunate enough to see any elephants - this wasn't a problem! We saw upwards of 50 wild elephants, ranging from 6 weeks old to fully grow males which we were told was quite rare to see. Definitely a must if you are in the area.
title: Nellys Everywhere!

body: Saw soooooo many elephants! And several up quite close too! But make sure to pay for yourself at the entrance, don't leave it to the tour guide as it'll be more expensive.
title: Beautiful!

body: I really wanted to see the Sri Lankan wild elephants, so I just ignored the experts opinion. Eventually I realised the consequence of my arbitrary decision. The best time to watch these wild elephant is July to end of September. But I went there in last December. But I was lucky enough to see dozen of elephants instead of hundreds. These Asian elephants are more beutiful than the African ones. Safari started early as 7am. The guide and park ranger was very knowledgeable and know exactly where can find the elephants. also we saw few peacocks, pelicans, some other birds. After all it was really remarkable safari, enjoyed the dry zone wild life in Sri Lanka.
title: Choose the wrong time of year

body: This place is famous among tourists as well as locals due to high population of elephants. Between May – October, the dry season is the best season to visit there.
title: Wild Elephants

body: Starting of with the negative, dozens of jeeps!Otherwise, beautiful area and elephants, elephants, elephants.You’ll get very close! So, must see when in the area, just don’t get bothered too much by the other jeeps.
title: Fantastic, dozens and dozens of elephants

body: No, not the elephants - the jeeps. I imagined a jeep safari would be a quiet affair, little did I know that all the jeeps set off at the same time, so we were virtually nose to tail the whole way round, unless we spotted some elephants and then we were 3 deep trying to take photos of them. Still, it was worth doing.
title: Nose to tail

body: Yes, we saw a lot of elephants. and more elephants. and nothing else, unless you want to count the egrets and storks...But... there were TOO MANY JEEPS. Easily 50 deep at every sighting watering hole. Way too many for any decent viewing or photographing. More than I have ever seen at any other game drive we have taken in the last 40 years. :(
title: Good Elephant Sightings. Nothing More and Too Crowded.

body: Yes, we saw a lot of elephants. and nothing else, unless you want to count the egrets and storks...But... there were TOO MANY JEEPS. Easily 50 deep at every sighting watering hole. Way too many for any decent viewing or photographing. More than I have ever seen at any other game drive we have taken in the last 40 years.
title: Too Crowded and nothing beyond elephants

body: Amazing, amazing - was so excited to be able to see the elephants and other wildlife. Tip...make sure you get a jeep that has proper tyres and that it is a 4x4......we saw two jeeps that couldn’t make it up the hill! There are various companies out there that offer a trip and all look pretty decent jeeps and the really good thing is that they respect the elephants space and keep to the track.
title: Excited

body: It is an excellent National Park. There is a large lake and we saw many birds. e.g. Paradise Fly Catcher and animals e.g. Elephants and Spotted deer.
title: Minneriya National Park

body: The park is definetly worth the money. We spotted many bird species, lizards, crocodiles, buffalos, monkeys and of course hundreds of elephants!But, at the moment there is no limited for amount of jeeps at the same time in the park creating massive traffic jams. That even led to a situation where the elephants could not cross their path! Please change the rules for jeeps and tourists to further protect wildlife
title: Great nature but too many jeeps

body: We visited the park whilst on an organised tour. I love to see animals in their own environment, they look so much happier. There are loads of elephants to see, water buffaloes and a variety of birds.The park is extremely busy with visitors and you can lose count of the jeeps.It is good there are tourists and especially if the money goes towards the upkeep and conservation.
title: Great to see animals in their own environment.

body: A very nice safari to see elephants. We went around 2:30 pm as it’s the time for elephants to come to the lake for drinking water. Our hotel was 50 minutes away from Safari point and cost us 60 US$ to pay the local jeep to take us around.
title: Very nice elephants safari

body: But it's worth the visit. The plains are beautiful and made more beautiful by the wild life. We saw herds of elephants, lots of peacocks (including one doing a dance and 2 others fighting), pelicans, etc. Amazing place
title: No, this is not Jurassic Park!

body: We were very early, at sunrise. We were the only ones in the park. We could see many birds, quite a few quadrupedes including elephants. No leopard and the like.
title: Very nice park

body: We went there around 2 pm and saw heaps of elephants - it was the best experience ever! I never saw elephants before in the wild life and it was amazing to see them. We went from Sigiriya and paid 5.000 Rupiah for our cheap but could divided it through 4. The entry fee for a group of 4 is 14.400 Rupiah but it is totally worth the money
title: Amazing trip to see elephants

body: We did manage to see elephants.. the attraction here... but the amount of jeeps racing around & jockeying for position was nasty! You’re just sucking gas fumes from dozens of jeeps around to see a group of elephants in the distance:(There’s needs to be a limit of vehicles per hour. Also have some etiquette where a few jeeps in front once you spent a few minutes take a few pics, move on & allow others to enjoy. So even though we did see elephants the experience left me disappointed! Mass Tourism at its worst!
title: Elephants.. Yes .. But..

body: Overcrowded but nice elephants to see near water with young ones. MANY jeeps rushing all over the place to position themselves for best position!
title: Overcrowded

body: All of the coach trips seem to do 10am and 3pm excursions, meaning the park is packed to the rafters with jeeps just after these times. We had a hired Tuk Tuk and so arrived independently. As soon as we arrived, we were approached by several jeep drivers, all offering to drive us for 2-3hours for Rs4,000. We chose a friendly driver, paid our entrance fee and entered the park.Our drivers English wasn’t incredible, but he was clearly interested in the wildlife and so we were able to converse well and we both thoroughly enjoyed the experience.As for the over-crowding with jeeps, we were on our own for a lot of our ride, with only the return journey being crowded by the incoming groups. Some of the drivers were clearly going off-track, but ours was conscientious. We were much happier with this wildlife park as opposed to Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage, which people kept recommending, as we felt that sitting on the elephants backs was inhumane.
title: Arrive at midday

body: We saw so many elephants on this trip. Unfortunately there are way too many jeeps too and some of the drivers hog their space if there is a good view.
title: So many elephants!

body: Minneriya is the best place to see elephants. You can see hundreds of elephants in Minneriya national park. Minneriya is the biggest elephants gathering national park. You can book a safari jeep and go closer to Elephants. You can see elephabts behaviours. All most all the of the tourist love elephants. This is one of the main activity all tourist love to do.
title: Biggest Elephants Gathering in Asia

body: What a beautiful place! Saw sooo many elephants and water buffaloes. Highly recommend visiting this park!
title: Amazing experience!!

body: We did a jeep safari tour as part of our Sri Lankan tour and we had the most fantastic day we say hundreds of elephants in their natural environment just doing what elephants do, there were several herds and we also saw some babies that were only a week or so old, we also saw water buffalo, and pelicans, deer and lots of other birds. It was a spectacular afternoon made all the better by our guides.
title: Fantastic afternoon tour

body: My wife and I visited here during our recent Birdwatching Tour of Sri Lanka 🇱🇰. We chose to take an afternoon Safari Drive as we’d heard that it wasn’t so busy then, hmm I’d hate to see how busy it was in the mornings 😂. Most people visit the park for the wild Asian Elephants 🐘 and they were impressive. However, our main interest was the bird life, which was extensive and impressive. Several rare and sought after species are easy to see here, Lesser Adjutant, Spot-billed Spoonbill, Paddyfield Pipit and Jerdon's Bush lark to name a few. The Asian Elephants 🐘 did steal the show. The place is a must for anyone visiting the area. Highly Recommended
title: Simply Stunning

body: Fantastic afternoon with the wife on a safari trip. Saw all sorts of birds, monkeys, lizards etc. But the highlight by far was seeing 200+ elephants all playing, eating and washing in the reservoir. Amazing experience!!!
title: Elephants, elephants and more elephants!

body: This is my 3rd time on Minneriya Safari and had different experiences each time. So you must be lucky enough as well to witness the best safari Life as well. You can go beyond the Water path and have a good experience only once I was able to go to that part. So talk with the driver to get the best experience. Mostly Elephants are there. lots of birds are available as well.
title: Good safari experience

body: Minneriya national park is a great place to see hundreds of elephants in a single place. This is where I saw the most number of elephants at a time in a single place. Best time to go is the evening as elephants come to the lake. Apart from the elephants you can see some other species like deer, wild boar, buffalo, etc. Be alert and get some information from your guide or any other local in the area about the crowd in the park as lots of crowd will ruin your experience.
title: An Elephant paradise

body: It was great to see such large numbers of elephants in the family groups - matriarch, babies, youngsters, teenagers. Then with the young males who had been kicked out from the herd just feeding a short way from the main herd. Interesting to watch the antics of some larger males finding their way into the smaller herds to check out the females. Yes there are a lot of safari jeeps but it did not seem as chaotic as in the Yala National Park and I think this is due to the fact that this park has a rather large open area of grass around lakes that allow for the army of jeeps to park by the road and allow for viewing by everyone as there were elephants everywhere. In Yala once an elusive leopard is found, it's a race on for ever driver to get their clients a sighting and the tracks are narrow and not as open as in Minneriya.I loved watching the babies, and yes the protective mothers keeping their bodies to the jeep side, but both continued grazing whilst we looked on. Watching elephant behaviour was interesting - a mother comin out from a bamboo thicket as we approached in the jeep. We stopped. She stopped. She waited - we didn't move. Then obviously when she thought it was safe, she signalled to the two younger elephants and one by one out of the thicket they came and crossed the track.I didn't feel the driver of our safari jeep hassled the elephants at all. All the jeeps seemed to give them the space. If the elephant came behind the jeep, the driver stopped, waited for the elephant to pass or do what it wanted, before the driver proceeded along the track The park appears to have designated trails that the vehicles can use and the jeeps generally stated on this track or to the side if they needed to pass.Its main purpose for this park I think is for wild elephant viewing, but we also saw lots of birdlife around the lake.We did an afternoon safari from 3pm and I found the seats were very nicely padded in our vehicle but seatbelts I think are optional, but then I was standing up a lot when the vehicle was parked or moving slowly along.It's not for everyone as it's hot, it's bumpy, but I enjoyed it.
title: Very exciting to see such large family groups

body: Did afternoon/ evening safari here. Over 250 elephant which we were able to get quite close to. Lots of young one too.Long queue to get tickets but our driver did the hard work for us Recommend for families as well as groups. All the children we saw seemed to be really enjoying it.
title: Elephant safari

body: I’ve to start acknowledging that my first experience on a safari was two years ago in Lewa Wildlife Conservancy Camp in Kenya, a stunning location with breathtaking game viewing and an outstanding respect for wildlife. Therefore, my standards before taking part in the Minneriya safari tour were very high. Having said that, I have to recognize I would never recommend this place to go on a safari. For many reasons. First of all, because you will start the tour with dozens of jeeps leaving at the same time. Then, the feeling that the safari is not meant to offer you an experience with wildlife by watching the animals in their natural habitat, but to give tourists the chance to get the snapshots they need to share with their friends on the social media. But the main reason I would advice to avoid this safari is that, although most of the jeep drivers (like ours) were professional and respectful to wildlife, some of them showed any respect at all for either the environment or the elephants. At one moment, we saw 5 jeeps off the road blocking a group of elephants, and preventing them no just from moving away, but from moving at all. If the park allowed less vehicles at a time and enforced stricter rules on how to approach the animals, as they do in other parks, it would be an enjoyable experience we all would benefit from.
title: Not a pleasant experience

body: We were at the afternoon safari which started at 3 pm and it was high season. The jeep had no seatbelts and the driver drove very dangerously so we had to hold on to the metal construction of the car. We were all sore at the end wirh our hands dirty from the rust. However, the main problem was that there were 100 jeeps (with 2 or 3 people) chasing 1 or 2 elephants. The area of the park is quite small, so imagine 100 jeeps racing to get the closest to the animal, going off the roads and through the jungle senseless. At one point the jeeps completely surrounded a mother with a baby. The jeeps didn't even turn off their engines and made so much noise. This is not ethical. This is not connecting with nature. This is not sustainable. This is taking advantage of animals and the environment. Yes, we saw elephants, and it was beautiful, but the animals were just numb and lethargic and no wonder why.
title: An awful experience

body: I went on an afternoon Safari as part of a Gate1 tour. The jeep guides knew the best places to see the elephants and we were not disappointed, seeing several herds both at a distance and close up. The park was extremely crowded though with a lot of jeeps, so if possible check with the locals first and try to go during a less crowded time. That aside, it was amazing to see all the elements in their natural habitat
title: The Elephants were amazing

body: We we’re staying in the park in order to reach sites within the cultural triangle, Sigiriya, Dambulla and Polonoruwa, it was amazing to see elephants in the wild even just walking down the highway great authentic experience.
title: Elephant Commute

body: "Very Unique Experience " plenty of wild life Elephants aplenty. Take plenty of water, caps, umbrella, binoculars, if possible. Beautiful scenery & birds. Booked our tour through Minihini Hotel. Thissa & his staff were FANTASTIC. Thank you guys.Cheers Glen W Melbourne Australia
title: "JUST ELEPHANTS & MORE ELEPHANTS"

body: I went in February. I think what I experienced there happens in most of the other parks close by like Minneriya or Kaudulla. Anyways he driver decided in which park the most elephants were expected. The few elephants there were surrounded by eight jeeps or more. The problem is that they don’t fill up the jeeps with people so there is mostly one Jeep per person or per couple. I understand that people need jobs here, but this is not a sustainable way and there are better systems in other National Parks. Jeeps crowd chaoticly around an elephant and sometimes the driver couldn’t get through or just drives by because there is no space to stop. Fumes and noise from the jeeps were constantly around me. I saw more animals outside in the country than in this NP. Not sustainable activity, no animals or nice nature observed, dusty, hot, polluted and crowded with people and Jeeps. Not recommended at all.
title: Bad!- More jeeps than animals

body: Our grand'children were delighted to see wild elephants, buffaloes, peacoks, big monitors and cameleons ...But the adults became annoyed by the traffic jam ! So many jeeps!...Better to be there at the low season....Anyway a bit of rain and mist made the scenery dreamy, beautiful. I suppose that we are a bit spoilt by many safaries in Africa.
title: No so big, almost cute !

body: Wow what a great after noon. Set off for a three hour safari and when we were finished we had seen approx 45 elephants in total. Many mothers with thier babies and a few old Tuskers. Very enjoyable and a must do.
title: Vacation

body: really remarkable. Take the evening visit - starts at 130 pm. Not too crowded and so many animals. Take you camera but you dont even need a long lens!
title: So many elephants -

body: Had a private safari tour of the park and we were not disappointed. There were Peacocks and Eagles in abundance and we also saw lots of small groups of elephants. Definitely worth a visit if you want to get up close to the elephants.
title: Fantastic meeting with the elephants

body: We saw a number of Elephants, Crocodile and Buffalo as well as some very rare birdlife. We had an afternoon and early morning safaris. Both worth while
title: Great small national park

body: We decided to add it to our trip on the way from Polonnaruwa to Sigiryia and did an afternoon safari. There were a ton of elephants and it was a fantastic experience. I think a jeep tour in a private jeep was $100
title: Excellent elephant viewing

body: I would not recommend this tour. Too many jeeps coming too close to the elephants. At one point, there were close to 20 jees surrounding a mom and her baby. The mom seemed frozen in her spot, and unable to move away due to being blocked by the jeeps. We had a park guide in our Jeep and we expressed our frustrations. While he seemed to understand to some degree, and even yelled at another Jeep to back up, he did not seem to teally take issue with what was occurring which was concerning given that he works for the park. I felt like I had engaged in an unethical experience following this tour.
title: Not animal friendly

body: We saw many elephants and other wildlife. the jeep was comfortable and convient for taking photos. The trip lasted almost 3 hours. Great value.
title: a great jeep safari

body: This experience was poor. Inexperienced drivers drived too fast to the elephants along with around forty other jeep drivers. I can tell here safari service is bad.
title: Poor

body: This was the worst safari I have ever experienced! Thousends of jeeps - in every jeep only two people. The jeeps don't stay on the roads. If they see elephants they drive wherever they want - without worries to destroy the National Park or if there might be nests of other animals. When they spotted elephants they regularly chase them and made circles with the jeeps around them. We saw lot of elephants, but the way we did so made me hardly cry. Please go to Udalawale to do a safari and not here - there they stay on the roads and respect the animals and nature! Please people in Sri Lanka - stop the way you treat the National Park and the animals - otherwise there won't be any tourists anymore
title: Don't support this - elephant chasing/ destroying nature

body: Cost a lot of money and not worth it. Far too many vehicles with drivers driving like mad men. Hardly saw and Elephant only in distance. In the morning driving on the highway one was right on side of road. No other animals either. Waste of US$100
title: Not worth it

body: We saw lots of elephants, and the park is a nice setting. I agree with some other reviews that, if it's busy, there are a number of jeeps, and you can smell the pollution from them, which made me feel bad about doing the safari. I used fasttur to book in advance. I am not sure whether they are overcharging or whether they charge the standard rate for entrance+jeep hire. But there is no visible benefit from their service, as you still have to wait for the driver to purchase the tickets. If there is a queue, that can be a while. But still, it guarantees you a jeep. They did say an English-language guide would be included, but that was not the case at all. In the end, you don't need one anyway, but I feel they should have given a discount for something they did not provide.
title: Good but could be better

body: We visited at 8am and only saw a few other jeeps in the park so completely contrary to some of the other reviews here. It took around 90 minutes to find an elephant. Apparently it usually takes only 10 minutes so we were unlucky. Once we found some the driver parked up around 50ft away whilst we watched them.We paid USD 90 for a private jeep for 2 people which our driver arranged. I suspect you could get it cheaper if you organised it yourself.
title: Visit in the morning

body: This experience was terrible. Inexperienced jeep drivers driving too quickly to the elephants along with around forty other jeep drivers. Avoid this not least to give the elephants some peace.
title: Awful experience

body: This was a terrible experience. They call it a jeep safari but it is mostly a jeep rodeo. Drivers jockeying to get close to the elephants. 30 jeeps surrounding 6 elephants revving their engines. Sad.
title: Give it a miss

body: Thoroughly enjoyed our visit. We must have seen between 80 -90 elephants, often in groups of 8 to 10, all females with young. The males are only around in June/July at mating time. We did get really close up to them and they did not seem in the least bit bothered by the jeeps and the elephants were not chased at all by the jeeps. The jeep ride is like a bucking bronco. We did not see nearly as many elephants in Yala. Don't bother with distant photos with half hidden elephants as you will see plenty up close.
title: The place to see elephants in the wild

body: Minneriya is renowned as a park in which to see elephant. We were lucky in seeing a large number around the open grassy shores of the eponymous lake. But beware! Do your local research before falling into the arms of the first jeep driver! The elephants move between three parks and are sometimes never here. Wonderful if you're lucky, but the large number of jeeps does not enhance the experience.
title: Potentially a fantastic elephant experience.

body: It's nice to see elephants here, in natural habitat and not in "prison" but apart from elephants one can see very limited number of other species (not only for our trip, but generally that's what we have heard).
title: Nice but not excellent

body: This was the most disappointing part of our Sri Lankan tour so far. Scores of jeeps kicking out fumes chasing the Elephant. No information given had no idea where we were going other than following other 4x4's .
title: convoy of 4x4's

body: Convoys of jeeps travel into the park in the search for wild elephants. Even though we were out of the gathering season, we saw several groups of elephants, including young babies, at very close range. It was fantastic.
title: Awesome experience!

body: Took a safari from our hotel. Most of the vehicles have up to four seats, and there are loads in the park all it appeared searching for the same herd of elephants. It’s quite a physical experience as the dirt roads are bumpy, but well worth it. We had multiple encounters with single and herds of elephants. It’s a must do if you are in the area.
title: Great fun!

body: We got see elephants close up but, in hindsight, would have passed this up and just done the safari at Yala National Park. Yala has a lot more to offer.
title: Nice but nothing on Yala

body: Relatively smaller national park in sri lanka. Can visit from Habarana or Dambulla. Large number of elephants (in hundreds) can be seen in the evening, specially during dry season. Birds can be seen in the morning. Lots of safari jeeps are available in dambulla and habarana and relatively cheaper than other national parks.
title: Elephant watching

body: We had pre-booked our safari and met the driver at 3pm. It was busy going into the park but the jeeps soon dispersed. We saw loads of elephants, peacocks and monkeys.At times we met up with other jeeps and there seemed to be a lot of us but everybody needed to see the wildlife so naturally congregated. The elephants with babies crossed the road in front of us it was awesome.Kids loved the jeep and racing with some of the other drivers in some parts. Really great highly recommended afternoon
title: Amazing afternoon

body: Yes you will see elephants in their natural habitat, however you will also see too many jeeps surrounding them.At times it was a competition to see who could get closest to the elephants, this did startle and aggravate several of the elephants and as mentioned above it wasn't nice to see.The area itself was beautiful but far too busy.
title: Very busy, felt sorry for the elephants

body: This is one of three 'safaris' we did in Sri Lanka, and was by far the least enjoyable. It seems that there is little regard for the environment or the wildlife as a large number of vehicles thrash around a relatively small area. I had the feeling that the tour was not about the wildlife at all, but about giving tourists a four wheel drive experience - not what we signed up for. The park itself appears to be in a sad state with many invasive weed species; the roads are overused by the heavy vehicle traffic and poorly maintained. We saw a few elephants, but the experience was marred by the volume of jeeps jostling for position. We got much more enjoyment out of seeing wild elephants by the side of the road than we did on this tour - save your money.
title: Wouldn't recommend

body: So cute! We run And run into The jungle to find elephant... And thanks to our guide, we saw Them!!!! To do!
title: Wonderful!!!

body: So upset with the Safari this afternoon I agree with the man that lives in Kania it was a shambles. You’ll go in the same way all 20 to 30 James drive the ages see you feel you’re very distant into the park are you actually not gone that far when you get to see the elephants the James entrap the elephants so march it’s very upsetting. The tourists are revolting and do not respects the wildlife or nature. It was like being in a safari zoo back home Hone. I have been on proper Safari is in Africa where they look after the animals and do not have so many jeeps surrounding a wild animal. This is for tourists not for wildlife lovers
title: Safari trip

body: Most enjoyable part of the 14 day trip to Sri Lanka. Had bit of excitement with an elephant. Everyone should go on an elephant safari.
title: lots of elephants

body: This is one Safari experience you shouldn’t miss. If you’re in the region, then make it a point to keep aside a half-day for the tour. Do get a good guide-cum-Driver to take you around the park.The park doesn’t have many big animals, but the Elephants makes up for everything. They are practically everywhere & easily spotted.A great experience 👌
title: A Great Safari Experience

body: I was disappointed by the whole experience. I lived in Kenya for years and visited all the best parks (Serengeti, Masai Mara, Amboseli, Ngorongo...) so I know what a professional safari should be like.I did not have great expectations for this, but I hoped for a quiet drive, looking for animals at a slow pace. What I got was way too many jeeps traveling bumper to bumper, with drivers busy racing, rather than spotting animals. It was clear the driver was in no way interested in anything, but getting his cash for a ride as fast as possible. I understand that a certain amount of overcharging is always going on and I don’t mind too much, as long as it is a genuine experience. This was just a ripoff.When finally we reached a herd of elephants, the poor animals were already surrounded by way too many jeeps. It felt sad, with most tourists making too much noise and taking selfies with the elephants in the background. Really disheartening.
title: I felt sorry for the elephants

body: The whole experience is very staged and disappointing. The problem is that the vegetation is very high and dense in the park, so while you do see elephants and other animals, they are usually far in the distance and you can only see them through lenses or binoculars. Also the variety of what we saw was very limited. After about 2 hours, all of the jeeps then take you to a large look out point high on a hill. While it was beautiful, again you can only see animals far in the distance unless you get lucky. It all seemed very stage like a Disney-world, andino in the final scene. Don’t waste your money! We later went to Udawalawe National Park in the south and it was spectacular. we saw numerous animals and birds very close up. It also cost us far less...$30 per person compared to $50 in Minneriya.
title: Overated.....don’t waste your money

body: We Saw very special places.Great Tour and very friendly Guide. We can highly recommend Lalith Safari Dambulla
title: Lalith Jeep Safari Dambulla

body: We spent a couple of hours in a large 4 wheel drive viewing many elephants of all ages here. The terrain was interesting if a little boggy (it rained overnight).
