title: With a landrover to this park

body: Recently spent the afternoon at Minneriya National Park and it was truly worth it, we loved seeing the elephants up close and they looked so happy, we was extremely nervous about coming to Sri Lanka and seeing elephants being mistreated like they are in certain parts of the world with them being beaten etc to ensure that someone can have there 10 minutes off happiness to ride them so when there to see they wasn't being pestered as such just watched this is recommended.
title: A must see

body: We saw two large herds of elephant totalling nearly one hunderd when we visited. It was a wonderful experience. Watch out is that we were one of 30-40 jeeps all enjoying the experience. There are other reviews mentioning only a couple of elephants on show. If there are still 30-40 jeeps trying to view a small number of elephants then I think the experience would not be so great. We were lucky though and happy to recommend
title: wonderful if the elephants are there

body: Great tour with a Jeep into the park. Got to see a variety of animals in their natural habitat. A must see in this part of Sri Lanka.Additionally as a bonus and due to the fact that it was a day with heavy rain, we got to see a great and very entertaining river crossing by the different safari cars/drivers. It was like a mud rally with crazy action.
title: Worth the visit

body: Our visit to Minneriya park was very exciting as me and my girl never seen an Elephant in the wild. We thought we could see 10-15 elephants. But instead we witnessed Elephant gatherings of more than 200 in a herd! Can you believe friends. Andrea counted 197 near the main lake area.The elephants were the center of attraction in the safari, but you could witness warthogs large amount of birds and buffaloes. If you are a elephant seeker, it's the best place in Sri Lanka. A safari tour will cost around $ 40/- including entrance and safari jeep. You can share the jeep with nearly 5 fellow travelers and reduce the cost as well.
title: If you are a giant Lover, This is the place to go!

body: Lots of elephants and bird life. Get your driver to take you away from the large number of safari jeeps and you will have a lovely time Saw lots of different eagles all fishing and of course the large herds of elephants and water buffalo This safari will be as good as your driver makes it for you !
title: Large elephant herds

body: this is one of the best places in srilanka to see tha wild eliphants,sambar deer,water buffalo,wild cats and crocodiles.its possible to see large number of elephants hear. the best time to observe elephant herds is from 3.00pm to 6.00pm.we had a wonderful experience in minneriya national park...
title: amazing experience in srilanka

body: Our guide told us that we need to get into a jeep to access the park. We didn't expect that we will be sitting at the back of a bare roofed jeep without seatbelts onsite travelling at 70 miles per hour in a snaky road for over 30 minutes to reach the park itself.When accessed the park we had to drive for another 40 minutes in this busy track with jeeps overtaking each other, at first we were getting bored because there was just the occasional monkey here and there, an owl sitting up a tree in distance, lots of peacocks ..... but when we reached the elephant, it was worth the journey (if you are an elephant lover, this is a treat).I'm just amazed at the majestic sight of elephants, so to me it was worth it. My husband doesn't agree.After taking selfies from the back of the jeep, it was time for the dreaded jeep drive back to our car. Another hour or so to get back with my heart in my mouth at the back of the roofless, seatbeltless racing jeep. We survived the journey to write this review ;-)
title: Once you reach the area with elephant, it's worth it

body: "The Gathering" is when the elephants come together and hang out, for lack of a better word. Coming to Minneriya NP was a last minute decision and are we ever glad we did. You have to ride in your jeep about 1/2 hour to get to the ancient reservoir where the elephants are. But once you are there (with many other jeeps) you will see up to 300 elephants, or so we were told. We saw two groups of about 30 elephants each. And it's like weren't even there. Of course, they are used to the jeeps, so they just go about their business. We saw a very young one, about a week old. They were blowing their horns and wallowing in the water, along side water buffalo. Oh, what an experience, son't miss it!
title: Go and see 'The Gathering"

body: My girlfriend and I have done a private safari in this NP. We paid 95$ for about 3 hours, 60 minutes of which we were just driving to and from the park entrance from Habarana. The roads were in such a bad condition that it really hampered the possibility of enjoying the drive. Furthermore our guide could hardly speak any english and the car was neither very comfortable nor could you fasten the seatbelts. The view to the front is completely blocked by the chassis of the car.The wordt part of the safari was that while beinh on the spot with the most elephants to see, I counted 86(!) other safari cars on the hunt for photos, which made our experience worse.It might be partly due to the fact that we're spoilt from our south african safaris, but we were not content over all and would not recommend it. Besides, it was way overpriced for Sri Lanka.
title: Overpriced Safari and way too crowded

body: Friends of ours visited the park in the dry season so they saw huge herds of elephants. When we went, there was a small herd of about 25 elephants of all ages including about half a dozen babies. Our driver was able to park very close, about 10 metres from the elephants and we stopped there in the quiet...only a few jeeps were there...to observe. The elephants went in the water and played, they chased each other, they sprayed water at each other, the babies ran around and at one point they all began to feed. It was very quiet, with no sound except the ripping up of the grass and munching noises. At this point they came closer and closer to us...only a few metres. A wonderful experience!
title: Wonderful!

body: did safari lake breeze jeepes safari give good services more than 3hours spend national parck very good place
title: nathuer

body: We were impressed by the great numbers of elephants, at several spots throughout the park. It's easy to spot them on the plain fields (it's not a very bushy park) on their way to and from the water holes. Many species of birds to be seen as well. We didn't regret doing this jeep safari, despite the many other safari vehicles around at the same time (they all seem to enter the park around the same time between 14.30 - 15.00 h, and leave the park towards 18.00 h). It wasn't too bad, though, not nearly as bad as in the Yala National Park (see separate review) which park should be avoided at all costs!! Here in Minneriya we were at least not completely fumigated by the many diesel Jeeps.
title: lots of elephants, and lots of tourist too!

body: Probably the best 10k rupees we've ever spent. We saw large numbers of elephants at close quarters, water buffalo, a crocodile and wading birds and birds of prey too numerous to mention, all in the most beautiful and natural of settings. We managed to see all this before the afternoon crowds arrived so there were only a handful of vehicles accompanying us on our safari. Our guide was polite, enthusiastic and knowledgeable and had keen eyes. More time to sit and observe might have improved our two hour experience though.Our driver on the other hand put his vehicle through its paces and gave us the bumpiest of bumpy rides. He was also in a hurry to return, presumably to pick up his next fare. He then became awkward over his tip or in his case, lack of one!So get the right driver, take your time and you should have an unforgettable experience.
title: With the right driver it's the best 10000 rupees you will ever spend.

body: First time for us seeing Asian Elephants in the wild. The vehicles were designed for viewing. The road leading in and out was very long and bumpy.
title: Great viewing of Asian Elephants in their natural setting

body: We did an afternoon jeep safari as part of a Sri Lankan coach tour. As such we didn't have to take a chance on our guide/driver as we would if independent. Our driver was sharp-eyed and knowledgeable, spotting and identifying birds at a distance and stopping to let us take photos. It seemed that other jeeps were just driving as quickly as possible to the "hot" elephant spots.You do have to be prepared for a bumpy ride but being close up to elephant families is special and worth the discomfort. If you are interested in birds, look out for Indian Rollers, Painted Storks, Grey Headed Fish Eagles and Little Green Bee-Eaters.We did a similar jeep tour of Yala NP later in the tour and much preferred Minneriya (see separate review).
title: Great experience, close encounters with elephants and lots of bird species

body: We booked this at the last minute and didn't know what to expect. There was a fair amount of jeep driving including at 60KPH++ without seat belts. It was quite expensive but you certainly get to see elephants - loads of them, and you can often get very close. Only problem as others have said, is if there were 100s of elephants there were probably 100s of landrovers too! They have to stop one person per vehicle as the number was crazy. So it is worth doing - just!
title: Elephants galore

body: Visited whilst touring, saw so many elephants , what an experience in the jeeps too, we had a great driver who stopped to allow us to take photos and pointed out wildlife
title: Fantastic experience

body: Whilst wanting to see elephants our interest in wildlife is much greater. A real shame that our guide and driver couldn’t identify many of the bird species, got many wrong from our limited knowledge and didn’t have a pair of binoculars between them. And seeing 20 jeeps around a few elephant is very sad.National Parks need to learn from East Africa
title: Elephants seen

body: Despite what the guide books are saying, you should go in the afternoon which is the best moment to see the elephants near the Lacs. We went at 6am and got lucky through the end to see 10 of them. However we saw lot of birds and other animals
title: Should have gone in the afternoon

body: A great park for a half day game drive - a beautiful place and plenty of elephants. We saw about 50 or so, along with buffalo, numerous birds and a HUGE water monitor. This thing was like a kimono dragon, easily 5-6 feet long. Well worth a visit.
title: Elephants galore

body: Wow what an amazing experience. We were lucky enough to have a very experienced ranger in the jeep with us and he took us to some of the quieter areas where we could see the elephants close up with less other jeeps around. We saw so many females, babies and even some males in the distance. We also saw some interesting birds and a few crocodiles. Definitely worth a visit.
title: Fabulous

body: We chose to come here over Yala national park as we heard Yala was quite crowded. We chose to go with Lake Breeze Guest house for our jeep and he knew a great local guide. We were able to see herds of elephants as well as lots of birds and other animals.
title: Amazing park

body: We were lucky to see many elephants close by. Our guide Warner was very informative. The animals have 200000 acres to roam. Did spot quite a few birds. The four wheel drive experience was also fun!
title: Wonderful

body: Visited with a guide/ safari jeep, and a promise that we would see lots of elephants.Lost count after 100- all different family groups, some large, some just 3 or 4.The jeeps drive and park close enough for great viewing and photos. Drivers respectful of the animals, and move on if the elephants seem bothered by their presence. Also saw lots of birds including Eagles nesting, pelicans, kingfisher and heron.
title: Elephants galore

body: A good place to visit to see the elephants but beware of the park guides who can choose any vehicle to get in, normally the ones who they think they can get the best tips from and your driver has to do as they tell him.
title: Lots of elephants

body: I would definitely recommend this national park for anyone new to Sri Lankan wildlife and is hoping to see some elephants. You are likely to see lots of them, and at close quarters. Other likely encounters are buffalo and a wide variety of birds. You will be in for a rather bumpy, dusty ride and be prepared for seeing many other tourists. The natural landscape is lovely and a good experience for travelers of all ages who want to get off main roads and see something of the natural environment.Take sun protection and water.
title: Very busy and good for elephants

body: You have to pay both entrance fee to the park and the hire of a jeep so not cheap, ( what’s new) did enjoy this trip albeit very dusty and you get thrown about a lot. Saw quite a few herds of elephants, some of the young were suckling their mother. You can get up quite close although obviously you can’t leave the jeep. Also water buffalo and we were lucky enough to see an eagle. Can you class this as a safari? I’ll leave it up to you
title: Good experience

body: Not only did I see many elephants, grazing, showering and playing in the lake, I also very much enjoyed the ride in the jungle. It felt very much like being in an unspoilt natural environment.I took an afternoon safari, which was relaxed and not too busy, with not too many jeeps. Make sure you check your allocated car for comfort and maintenance before you hand out your money.
title: A rewarding experience.

body: We enjoyed our afternoon but a safari it wasn't. It felt more like a wildlife park/zoo. There were way too many jeeps, completely surrounding the elephants, I felt sorry for them. The park needs to limit the number of jeeps or regulate it a bit better. As other people have said it is very bumpy and dusty - ladies wear a sports bra if you can! We were lucky to see some golden jackals and the bird life was fantastic.
title: Nice but not a safari

body: We had a fantastic experience in our open top jeep. It was great sunny conditions and arrived at 3:30pm which was good timing to see the wildlife grazing.
title: Amazing lush landscape to see herds elephant in the wild

body: Our local driver/guide took us here to experience elephants, buffalo and other wildlife in this beautiful conservation park. Highly recommended as you go in small groups.
title: So close you can almost touch them

body: I had to select the kind of trip as "Family with teenagers", however I visited this National Park with my parents (I am 27 years; no longer a teenager).Needless to say, you can visit this park withs small children and teenagers as well.My images do not do it justice; my iphone broke before the trip but I could save one!
title: Amazing, must see!

body: So many elephants, our guide advised there were up to 300 in the herd.This was very well organised, although very popular so literally hundreds of tourists in 50+ vehicles, which does detract a little.Otherwise really enjoyed the 1/2 day trip.Note: Don't wear good clothes, we got a little dirty from mud kicked up when 4-wheel drive went through a muddy patch, all good fun.
title: Excellent sight seeing experience

body: We went with 7 adults and 1toddler. Hired a open Jeep . The vehicle cost was LKR 3000 for approximately 2 hours and we separately purchased entrance tickets. The ride was superb on bumpy roads we saw herds of elephants, foxes , Eagles and many birds. An officer from the wild life department accompanied us and gave us loads of information on the park. Only advice is if you are trancelike with young children, keep them in the middle and hold them tightly as the ride is bumpy and since it goes even between herd of elephants in case the driver has to speed during an emergency.
title: Amazing experience

body: As we visited during the Christmas period, there were a lot of jeeps! It felt rather invasive of these animals home. Thankfully for the animals, the jeeps stayed a respectful distance. The driver explained that many of the animals were not coming out, due to the high volume of traffic. We were able to see several elephants, some birds and that was it. The nature itself was beautiful, so it was a pleasure to drive around. From what I understand, other parks have more variety of animals.
title: Impressive elephants and some birds....nice drive.

body: Multiple elephant sightings are practically guaranteed here. Although there are huge numbers of jeeps in the park, especially during afternoon/sundown, the drivers appear to be less cowboyish in attitude and more sensible than their Yala counterparts. A vehicle in good shape and a skilled driver took us across muddy river beds to reach areas of prime elephant viewing. Apart from these pachyderms, there are buffalo and birds (notably peacock) and the drive through the bush is itself quite pleasant. Headgear and sun-screen are musts!
title: Elephant high!!

body: We choose to take the jeep safari. It was well worth it. We saw three different herds of elephant, so very close feeding from the grass and also be able to see how the young ones are copping. Really recommend this visit.
title: Recommended

body: I was surprised by the amount of elephants. It was so nice to see all the elephants from so close by. The Jeep tour was amazing and I would definitely recommend it.
title: Many elephants

body: Our guide had arranged a jeep 10km away from the park. It is a bumpy ride sitting on bench seats so not for those with bad backs. Part of the trail is through woodland then grass land areas. We saw three large herds of elephants quite close to as well as cows, a crocodile and quite a few birds. However is was very hot with no shade in our jeep.
title: Very hot but definitely worth visiting

body: Pick the right time so,it's not too busy and this is a wonderful place to see literally hundreds of wild elephants
title: Elephant paradise

body: That place amazing . You can see the reality of elephants life.from the tamarind resort 15 minutes by jeep . I can recommend to you this place highly..!!!
title: Safari

body: Group: 26 people of all ages from babies to seniors.. in 4 cars Price: 45$ for adult , half for children 6-12 and less than 6 free of charge + 1000R tips per car Recommended; highly recommended, amazing experience.Duration: 2 to 3 hours Animals: birds and elephants , elephants and elephants, you are up close to this beautiful animal in natural surroundingsExperience: we loved it Weather was amazing Cars in. Very good condition Not crowded at all Got to see : mother& baby elephant ,many Times we saw a very big herd of elephants and we Could get very close to themThe view and the area is so beautiful that you enjoy the ride even in the parts that you are not spotting the animals Notes: we went to Yala as well,we all preferd Minneriya and found Yala over rated
title: Highly Recommended

body: This was our first time in this park. I have to say whilst I highly enjoyed the experience. To see the elephants in the wild was amazing. Our tour guide was very informative regarding the elephants also.I did feel some of the drivers got on and some of them were lose cannons. One driver over took us when we were heading back and nearly caused an accident. Some very dangerous driving this even compared to Sri Lankan driving as a whole.Well worth going to. One of the highlights for us during our trip to Sri Lanka
title: Jeep Safari

body: We took a jeep safari through Minneriya and really enjoyed it. However, our driver didn’t risk getting across the riverbed as lots of jeeps were getting stuck in the mud - this curtailed the experience a little. We did see many elephants roaming in the wild and the bird-life is also prolific. There are a lot of jeeps on the trails which can make it somewhat congested, however, I’d still recommend a visit. Udawalawe was actually our preferred safari and we hope to visit Yala in the future.
title: Wild elephants galore!

body: Visited here on a country your with my wife. Our guide had told us about the number of elephant that we might see, but I was a but scheptical but i should not have been! We went in a jeep and after about half an hour found ourselves at the side of a huge lake with around 200 elephant in front of us. What I will say is that it is very popular - there were several dozen other jeeps there too, but to be honest they all seemed to behave pretty sensibly and didnt get to close to the elephants. For their part they seem pretty oblivious to our presence and happily ate and played like we werent there. A fab experience and real highlight of our trip.
title: Wow!

body: Bumpy ride. We must have had the oldest jeep. We saw many groups of elephants, about 60 in total. Amazing experience. Brilliant driver and guide. Highly recommended.
title: Fantastic afternoon

body: We thoroughly enjoyed our safari. The park is very beautiful. We were able to see an abundance of elephants. It was just amazing for us to see the elephants so close up. An unforgettable experience.
title: Great Experience

body: OK. So you've probably got big expectations of this park. It definitely has lots of elephants, particularly late August and September when the famous 'Gathering' takes place. It is probably almost certain that you'll see elephants any time of the year.But here's a reality check for you: the Jeep 'safari' that you've got in mind almost certainly will involve your Jeep and around twenty or thirty others that all jostle for position as soon as an unfortunate elephant is sighted. We're talking here of revving engines, other jeeps parking between you and the elephant so you can't see it. You're going to be one of maybe 100 gawking tourists.We were actually caught in a traffic jam in the park! Horrible!This is unsustainable tourism. The Jeep drivers are not quite cowboys but close to it. There is no time or room for contemplating the wonders of nature in silence because all you'll here are revving engines. You might as well go to a zoo.We were extremely disappointed by our experience. All I can advise is to lower your expectations to rock bottom - or simply don't go. It isn't what you might think it is.
title: Very disappointing and depressing

body: We visited the park on a short 3/4 he safari trip. We saw lots of interesting birds. The highlight was the elephants. There were around 150 that we saw in total and it was amazing to see them in the wild. They are magnificent.Our driver was good too. Definitely worth a trip if you haven’t seen elephants in the wild before.
title: Hundreds of elephants!!

body: We been few times to Minneriya, Always guaranteed to see elephant if you go right time of the day.Be aware of the safari truck mafia
title: If you want to see Elephants this is the place

body: Had a lovely tour Went around 3pm saw one water buffalo and then lots of elephants Bumpy roads. Lots of dust and dirt which is understandable you are in nature and the paths/road is dirt because your in the elephants natural habitat
title: Went on a Jeep tour

body: If you want to watch people on safari get too close to the poor wildlife then this is the place to go! There is no quota on jeeps and the result is disgusting. For some reason I can’t access the photos through the trip advisor app otherwise I would post them
title: So bad

body: I wouldn't classify this as a real safari, it was just an elephant viewing area that was jam packed with jeeps all trying to get a close up with the elephants. I was expecting to see some water buffalo or deer or pigs but it was only elephants and birds. Seeing the herd of elephants was neat but I got bored after 3 hours of it with nothing new to see. I think that for the price it is not worth it.
title: Elephants

body: Excellent location to view elephants in their natural habitat. We saw around 75 of them as well as numerous tropical birds. Recommend going before the busy 3-6pm window as the park fills up with safari jeeps late in the afternoon.
title: Elephants!

body: My run with safaris has never been great, with barely an animal or 2 in sight. But Minneriya was a sight to behold! You hire a jeep (try to make advance bookings if you are going there on a weekend or national holiday because they tend to book out really fast) that takes you right into the national park near a lake where elephants of all sizes congregate in hoards! We went in the afternoon slot and saw tons of them - any photographer’s dream
title: 100s of elephants!

body: A wonderful experience- while the guide couldn't guarantee we would see any elephants at all, we say 2 huge heards! It was a magical experience and would highly recommend.
title: Lots and lots of elephants!

body: Minneriya wasn't on our original itinerary, as we focus more on seeing the archaeological and religious sites. However, we found a gap in our schedule, and our excellent guide from Sri Lanka Personal Drivers set up a safari for us in a private 2 seat Jeep.We went around 1:30 in the afternoon, and it ended up being the perfect time (on the way out, we saw dozens of jeeps coming in, while we were the only one heading out). This also meant we had a five minute line for tickets, whereas the day before apparently had been an hour+.The first 20 minutes inside the park is just getting to the location, so you don't see much. But once it opens up, it was astonishing. We saw 3 distinct groups of elephants, each numbering 40-50. At times we were mere feet away. From not on the itinerary, it became easily one of our top experiences in Sri Lanka.Be aware that the elephants do tend to move around, so ensure you get word on whether they are more located at Kaudulla or Minneriya during your visit. We overheard other folks over dinner the night before saying they only saw a dozen or so Elephants at Kaudulla.
title: Astounding - 150+ Elephants Up Close

body: This was a fun few hours in a ‘Safari Jeep’ getting up close to the elephants. We got some great pictures and our driver did his best to get us really near to the elephants, as did all of the other drivers. At times it felt more like being part of a herd of jeeps watching a much smaller herd of elephants. There wasn’t much else in the way of wildlife to see other than some interesting bird species, so overall definitely worth a visit to see lots birds and elephants but not what I would consider a true safari experience.
title: An up close look at the elephants

body: What an amazing experience, travelling through the jungle in a Jeep. We got too see peakcocks, pelicans, other birds and elephants. Great place to take photos and create memories.
title: Amazing Experience

body: Took a risk and went in the morning when the elephants could have been less visible. For the first hour we didn’t see any other jeeps in the park. Early on saw deer, buffalo and peacocks. Eagles, storks, cranes as well. Finally saw the herd of elephants. We’re about 30 or so by the water including a few young ones. Kept a respectable distance away. Spent 20mins watching them before the next Jeep bumped along. Magical. A single male was also visible about 1km away. We drove around to see him a bit closer and then came across another 10 elephants moving through the scrub later. Finally a crocodile on the track that moved quickly into the water and some some wild monkeys sealed it for us. One of the highlights of our Sri Lankan trip.
title: Well worth it

body: Visit in the early morning to see the park waking up. Plenty of Elephants for the jumbo watchers, and much easier to see and observe than other parks. A large variety of birds and other wildlife too, and somehow the sanctuary seems much more relaxed. The Minneriya tank is a definite plus, with the migratory birds found in large numbers in and around the water. The trackers and guides are helpful too, and quite knowledgeable about the trees and herbs unique to Minneriya.
title: A nearer alternative to Yala.

body: We had a great guide gave us enough time to capture the natural beauty of minneriya national park. We had a great time seeing elephants, local birds, Sri Lankan peakok & some monkeys 😊
title: The best nature jeep Safari to see elephant

body: Well worth doing - book a jeep and driver keep eyes peeled an you will see lots of wildlife and really large families of elephant.
title: Lots of elephant

body: Highly recommend visiting here, it is such an adventure! We visited mid November and were lucky to see over 50 elephants, an eagle and lots of different species of birds. There are a lot of bugs so be prepared to get bitten if they like you!
title: Amazing Adventure

body: Was such a great park. Saw countless elephants, all in different places. The drivers help each other out which is nice, so if there’s been a sighting you don’t miss out. Saw so much more than elephants too - monkeys, buffalo, bee eaters, monitor lizards, parrots, giant squirrels, countless birds!Get feedback from your guide which the best Park is at the time of your visit, I’m really glad we chose this one!
title: Saw so much!

body: We were very lucky to see so many elephants and different varieties of birds. There are a few jeeps but on our visit they kept a very respectful distance. Delightful experience
title: Elephants, elephants and more elephants

body: Headed into the park, all the drivers know where the elephants are, we restrained ourselves and saw monitor, storks, pelicans, egrets and a hawk before finding our own private spot to watch the herd of approximately 30 go about their daily ritual of feeding, drinking and the juveniles playing - testing their strength, particularly hysterical pushing themselves up and down the canals. Other vans joined as from time to time, particularly when the elephants came close. But we stayed and could hear them eating, communicating when the other vans moved on after a couple of pictures. 1000 elephant pictures to sort through!
title: Elephants, elephants and safari vans

body: If you like to watch elephants this is the place to visit.The best period of the year to visit is from July to October when the water around the area start to dry up. If you are lucky you can see 100+ numbers in a heard during that time.If you are going to visit this park and hire a safari jeep get a 4X4 and fix the price and minimum safari time of at least 2hrs.As it was the kids first visit to this park managed to show them around +/- 50 elephants including 3 young tuskers
title: Off season Safari to Minneriya National Park

body: 345 jeeps for a day.80% are tourists .but they just have one ticket counter.we cant find the staff .they dont have any uniform .staff at the tickets checking counter are just like a wild animals .
title: 345 jeeps for a day.80% are tourists .but they just have one ticket counter.we cant find the staff .they ticket counter

body: To see the wild elephant this is the perfect place. All we saw were elephants, many of them and babies which I had not seen before. I recommend this attraction either early morning or early evening
title: Elephant

body: Can't recommend this more highly. Plenty of birds, elephants and deer to see - great landscape and plants as well. Downsides are the number of jeeps on the clear plains and getting bogged/helping others that got bogged. Best to ensure your vehicle is a jeep, Toyota or Mitsubishi - not a Mahindra. Also best to ask your guides to take the road where there are less other vehicles - our first two hours were by ourselves, completely, and it was excellent. Was a little less impressive when we could see a 100 jeeps cramming in near the elephants on the open plains.
title: Great experience

body: Despite the many jeeps, there are lots of elephants, deer and wart hogs. The birds are amazing - the wild peacocks are a trip.
title: Great place to see elephants and birds

body: We visited mid november and I actually had no idea what to expect. I'd read nothing before we arrived and I had in mind that it was a little like going on safari in that I may see one or two elephants. In fact, the first elephant appears in the trees and I already thought that was wonderful. We turned around the corner and there, i front of us were around 60 elephants. An utter delight to see.Our guide seemed quite savvy and when everyone else was getting closer and moving in one direction, he shot off in another and round the corner, we then saw around 200 elephants....Just amazing. Such beautiful intelligent creatures. We watched families, babies, older and younger playing. We saw dynamics between different elehphants. We saw them eating and when some moved to the water hole, we saw them drinking too.I notice that some of the reviews say that they only saw a couple. There could be hundreds, as we saw, but they could be on another part of the park as they do like to walk and wander. My advice would be to do your research on the guides. Ours was certainly in contact with others to find where they were. Ours came through our Sri Lankan guide via Aitken Spence.
title: Elephants galore!

body: We went there mainly to get a closer look at a large group of wild elephants (generally there should be 200+ elephants). But sadly, there was like 10 elephants in different isolated locations and we were not able to get close to them. (though we spotted a deer and a few birds). Because of the rain, the elephants were not required to come to the lake for grass or water. And the mud made the jeeps stuck preventing going to further areas.According to the driver, the best period to spot elephants is April to August. And we should get into the park around 2.30 pm. And most of the safari jeeps are 2WDs. Try to find yourself a 4WD if it’s rainy season.We went to kaudulla national park on the following day, because we really wanted to get closer look at the elephants. And there we found about 60-70 elephants.The cost for minneriya was : Rs. 3000 + charges for ticketsThe cost for kawdulla was : Rs. 4000 + charges for tickets
title: Surprisingly no elephants

body: This park has to be one of the best option in Sri Lanka to see a lot of wild elephants. We atleast encountered a hundred of elephants with a baby elephant which was around 7 days old according to the guide. A must visit when in Habarana.
title: It's fun to see wild elephants in the jungle

body: Incredible number of elephants. Saw hundreds including babies. Fantastic opportunity to get up close. Also lots of birds and few buffalo, but this is all about the elephants.
title: Lots of elephants, lots and lots of elephants!

body: We spent a few hours driving around the park just before sunset one evening. We saw in excess of 100 elephants in separate groups, some came within a few feet of our jeep! We also saw eagles, peacocks and many other birds. Having seen captive elephants in Thailand this was a treat and very special.
title: Safari trip

body: i just loved this park. I cannot yet decide whether this or Wilpattu is my favorite in Sri Lanka, among the parks I have visited so far, but it is definitely the number one destination if you love elephants. if you do not, you will fall in love with them after a visit in Minneriya. It is impossible to stay indifferent to these magnificent creatures. You can meet as many as 300 elephants at the same time up close, and the location is great too: wide spaces, huge lake, so plenty of birds around as well. It will not take more than 4 hours, but, wow, what a great time you will have there. Guaranteed...i also suggest that you book it when you arrive, not online. ask for the advice of locals, they know better, or the place where you are staying (just note 4-5 star hotels will charge much more than the direct prices).
title: Amazing encounter

body: A must-do! Our jeep driver was very good and we had it to ourselves so plenty of room to see everything clearly. Saw lots of elephants including two large herds with tiny babies! They were very entertaining. We got caught in torrential rain and lightening which went on for most of our safari but it just made the elephants more active and playful as they were loving the rain! An amazing experience.
title: A great experience!

body: If all you want to see are Elephants this is your best shot. The vast open spaces makes going up to the herds really easy. It isn't a waiting game like Yala or Wilpattu. Theyr'e just out there in the open usually.
title: If all you want to see are Elephants this is your best shot.

body: Our elephant safari was booked at one of the many roadside vendors but ours came recommended by our trusty driver. The Mahindra Bolero 4x4 picked us up from our hotel and took us to the Minneriya National Park where our guide was very quickly pointing out exotic wildlife to us… kingfishers, Peacocks, Crocodiles, water buffalo, monkeys and of course the Elephants. The Elephants were the highlight of the tour, initially seeing a solitary bull elephant and then shortly thereafter seeing a herd of around 70 elephants of all ages travelling down to the waters edge of the Minneriya reservoir. After taking hundreds of photos of this magnificent herd in brilliant light conditions we moved to find a smaller family group of 5 elephants and then later a mother large herd of around 60+ elephants. It was an absolutely awe inspiring sight seeing these magnificent creatures up close in the wild like this. Be aware though that yours is not the only jeep on the safari… at one point the number of 4x4s exceeded the number of elephants! The drivers are all aware of the issues this poses and do their best to avoid driving into one another shots
title: A real treat for Elephant fans

body: It was lovely to see two herds of wild elephants and a couple of lone bulls. It was an interesting experience and getting stuck in the mud and having to be towed out was a first!
title: Very good

body: The Park is covers a huge area and the only way to access the park is by way of Jeep which can be hired to drive you through the park. It is too hot and humid to walk and I could see that there were no hikers on foot. I believe that the Park authorities do not permit anyone to go in without a guide or on foot.
title: Amazing Park in its Natural habitat

body: Well we only saw two elephant families, so all together about 10 elephants. Then there was small birds and buffalo's. I was keen on seeing herds of elephants, but our guide said that this is not the time.
title: Just birds, buffalo's and not that many elephants

body: Minnerya Wildlife Park where you can see at close range large herds of wild elephants and water buffaloes gathering and feeding openly and enjoying themselves free in nature. Wonderful sight. Kids and family will love it. Where else can you see such large herds simply gathering in such free and easy manner openly relaxing in natural environments. Worth every cent. Please do not miss this place if you are visiting Sri Lanka. Be awed by the experience
title: Amazing Place To Visit

body: Minnerya and Kadulla National Park is vast and beautiful. So many varieties of birds. Excellent place to see large herds of wild elephants and water buffaloes gathering and feeding openly and enjoying themselves free and at peace with nature. Astounding experience just to enjoy these animals close. A truly must see experience for the entire family especially kids who will have fun and learn the beauty of these wild herds GATHERINGS. Highly recommended worth every cent. Please do not miss this wonderful educational family experience
title: The Gathering

body: If you want to see elephants this is the place to visit. However the gatherings are seasonal (May to September as I can remember). The hotels nearby will arrange visits for you. A must visit !
title: The best elephant gathering in Sri Lanka

body: Five of us took a safari here which involves being driven through the park in an open FWD accompanied by a guide.October is the shoulder season, before the monsoon which means there are still plenty of elephants to see in the park but not the big crowds of the high season.It is a beautiful park. After a 30 minute drive through the jungle/forest and spotting a minute lizard, chameleon, monkeys and several bird species, the park opens up to a huge plain which in the wet is mostly a lake. In the dry the lake is smaller but still significant. Apparently 300- 400 elephants come down to the lake-side at the height of dry season in August to drink. We saw a herd of about 30 with many babies, and two other smaller beards plus a few bulls, one up close.We were able to get fairly close to the large heard and there were at most three or four other vehicles, so everyone had a chance to see. The baby elephants frolicked and fed making for great photos and video. There was also a large herd of water buffaloes and many pea cocks and hens. Also some interesting bird life.The ride is a little rough especially if you stand rather than sit which we did for the view. But this would only be a problem for the very frail. Our guide was very helpful and knowledgeable. About $US 30 a head for a bit over two hours is great value.
title: Beautiful park

body: We went there wwith an agency from sigiriya, hinestly I think it's better to go on place and to get a jeep directly at the entree, there are a lot and they waiting for people... prices should be better. We had luck, we've seen soooo many elephnats, also crocodiles, chameleones, differnets kind of birds, bees, etc... honestly if you ever been in this corner of the world, nothing amazing for animals excepting elephants, and just for that... it woth it! You have to check before where they are as they moving during the year (3 differents park). If you have a guide he could do this for you. If you're doing the same as us, you have to know that you can negociat the prices, we had 2500 roupias less on the price as we show the routard guide telling it should be cheaper...
title: Elephant

body: Was a fantastic experience visiting the national park and seeing elephants in their natural habitat! After visiting an elephant sanctuary in Thailand and hearing the horrible things done to elephants to 'domesticate' them, I couldn't think of any worse than seeing a show or riding an elephant therefore it was amazing to be able to see them, how they should be, in the wild! We did also see monkeys, a crocodile and some bird life too but we saw so many families of elephants!My one criticism would be that their doesn't seem to be a limit on the amount of jeeps let into the national park at any one time and some get very close to the animals to the point of being intrusive but otherwise I would highly recommend a trip to this park.
title: Fabulous experience, elephants, elephants, elephants!

body: The scenery itself is stunning, vast open plains with a beautiful lake.If you don't mind the sun (3-4 hours drive in open fields) go open-top. Elephants are everywhere in herds. There are the occasional crocodiles and monkeys, if you are lucky leopard too.
title: Elephants, crocodiles, monkeys etc.

body: This trip was amazing. We were so well looked after. We had our own jeep and did no0t feel rushed throughout the trip but we able to enjoy the tour. We saw so many elephants. I'm talking maybe 50 or so. In their natural habitat. It was amazing to watch them behaving naturally. There are also numerous birds and other wildlife to see. Definitely make this part of your holiday!
title: IF YOU LOVE ELEPHANTS GO HERE!

body: We enjoyed a 4 hour safari in an open jeep. Bumpy road- but great fun. The jolts were more than compensated for by the sheer magic of seeing 6-8 herds of wild elephants (about 160+). They ranged in size from babies to 40-50 year old adults. Other animals were storks, Ibis, Egrets, Eagle, Iguano, buffalo, cattle & lots of birds. Fantastic!
title: Elephants in the wild!

body: The sole purpose of my trip to Sri Lanka was to see the annual elephant "GATHERING" that takes place in this park. It happens because of the dry weather and the ellies come here for water and green grass. WELL....this year Mother Nature decided to give them plenty of water so there was no drought and therefore NO GATHERING>>>!!! Oh well, I knew in advance that nature does what nature wants to do and not what tourists want it to do. Nevertheless, I had some fine ellie viewing anyway. Not huge herds as I had hoped, but good stuff anyway. I had some very good photo ops with the ellies and came away happy.
title: No "Gathering"....good ellie viewing anyway..........

body: Had been to this Park while on tour in Srilanka. The Entrance with the Jeep type at the gate and the entire worthiness of it doesnot go hand in hand. The entrance is exhorbitantly costly, advisable if a bargain is striked with the Jeep driver of the park else it is a complete Drain on ones pocket and timein this Park. One has to be prepared to get a very sad upkeep of the park as if deteriorated by insiders of its greens and woods, as well as there is no such proper fauna and flora for the animals to be part of this park. this view is as compared to one in tour in south africa or Kenya. The entire park area is sadistically barren, hardly any Animals to be spotted and one gets completely drenched out in the scorching sun with no beautiful aura of the entire park as such. pleas emake sure to cancel out this unadvisable, uneconomical and time wasting trip that has no value when the management itself has no interest in the upkeep of Animals and its flora and Fauna compared the country being full of green flora and fauna else where in wild. The ride itself is very dangerous as drivers are not of that calibre or disheartened at their Jobs. Am apologising for this negative review to help many before investing time into this journey. worthy is to visit Africa if for animals in wild and in variety.
title: Not worth the Time and Money Spent in doing this Ride

body: A great safari. We saw lots of elephants. My only negative is that the National Park allows so many jeeps into the one zone. There doesn't seem to be any control over the way some jeeps are driven when trying to get close to the elephants.
title: Elephants, Elephants

body: Arranged for a 6 am jeep safari. Had a great guide from the national park service who pointed out all the interesting birds and had the driver stop so we could take photos. Saw two male elephants up close. He said the morning safari allows you to see more wild life and the afternoon safari departing at 2:30 brings you to The Gathering which has more elephants. We thought this was a spectacular experience. Departs at 6 am and returns at 8:30. Take a look at the museum too.
title: Great safari

body: Wonderful experience spending time with the elephants in their own back yard. Far too many Jeeps attending at once and some getting too close. I'm pleased to say that ours kept its distance. The elephants did on occasion react to those who were infringing a little too much on their personal space.
title: It's all about the Elephants

body: The elephant safari here really is as good as it gets, we saw around 100 elephant who passed us within a few meters of the Jeep. Guides were experienced and very friendly. During the 3 hour safari We also viewed water buffalo, monkeys and various birds but it's the elephant experience that we will remember.
title: Don't miss this opportunity - amazing Elephant safari

body: We had an amazing time visiting Minneriya National Park and saw over a hundred elephants. Definitely recommend !
title: Loads of elephants

body: Had a lovely experience, we saw a number of asian elephants close up and spent a good amount of time with them.The visit was not part of our itinerary booked through Southall Travel, it was an "extra" arranged with our driver. We paid 10 thousand for the vehicle plus park entrance fees, as opposed to 5 thousand rupees paid by Simon B on his review dated 17th August. Hence the word of caution re: fees.
title: Nice, but we may have been ripped off?

body: Safari jeep ride into Minneriya. I thoroughly enjoyed the whole experience and would recommend to everyone visiting this area. Ok, it felt a little bit like a UK safari park at times, following a set route and with lots of other jeeps around. We saw 2 elephants, 1 up close and probably only 20 feet away. A memorable experience.
title: A memorable experience

body: We went on a safari to catch a glimpse of elephants in the wild. With a good driver and 4x4 vehicle, you will be able to spot a couple of herds and get a lesson on the lifestyle of these magnificent animals. The landscape is African-like, and the Jeep ride loads of fun. However, bring a hat, a good sunscreen and a pair of binoculars. You will, unfortunately, do as much people watching as animal watching, both being equally fascinating.
title: Great experience

body: As a family of four we took a jeep with The Elephant Voyage from Habarana. They were introduced by our driver and met us at the park gate for an afternoon visit (we were staying in Polonnaruwa). Jeep cost 5000 rupees, park fees were separate.It was a dry overcast afternoon, we started shortly before 2pm and we saw one lone elephant and one group of elephants together with a selection of other wildlife. I was a little disappointed but it was early in the season and our driver did his best by getting us to the right place at the right time. The drive through the park was fun and me and our 13 year old enjoyed standing up and looking out/ducking tree branches as we went along.
title: 8 August - Some elephants

body: This was a 2.5 hour safari where we booked the jeep in advance which saved us Rs2000 to just showing up. Our guide knew what he was doing and took us to a place without any other jeeps around. We saw a lovely group of elephants with some baby elephants - great experience. We then went to a place with more elephants, but I counted 50 jeeps and approx 45 elephants. Did not feel as nice as the first encounter. All in all, great experience with guaranteed elephant sightings, so good for kids..
title: Elephants

body: Sad experience as we didn't get to see a single elephant in about 2.5 hrs spent here. Our driver picked us up at 6 am from our hotel in Sigirya in jeep and drove us to Guadala national park whereas we had talked on Minneriya. We rerouted for Minneriya as we had heard so much of it on tripadvisor.. However didn't get to see a single elephant. The jeep experience was little pricey though lots of fun especially for my little daughter. I advice on checking with your agent first which park is best and at what point of time.
title: No Elephants

body: only to visit with a jeep tour; and their are too many of them. of course tourists want to see eliphants. but why are there many Jeeps with just to persons in the car instead of 6? why not small vans, so that more people can watch, with less vehicles.we saw that the eliphants were really disturbed, and even try to attack some jeepsAnd: in Sri Lanka you can see in a lot of places Eliphants, you don't need to go specially to Minneriya.the tour guides predict you will see 70 to 100 Eliphants take a bath, but because of all the Jeeps, the Eliphants couldn't reach the water and were waiting till 18.00 pm, when everyone needs to leave the park.we saw a few small groups of eliphants, all together maybe 40 eliphants. nice to see them in the wild and closeby, but we didn't feel really well about this visit.it disturbs the animals too much, park rangers try to handle this.
title: more jeeps than eliphants

body: It's worth getting up early to meet your jeep at dawn and be in the park first thing in the morning. It's cooler then and animals are up and roaming around before taking shelter from the heat later. Elephant families with babies, birds soaring over the plain, mongoose scurrying home with breakfast tight in its teeth, herd of gaur heading back from the lake, fish eagles diving ... The guides spot the animals long before you do, and patiently point them out until you spot them too. Excellent trip.
title: Never seen so many free roaming elephants!!

body: We joined a late afternoon safari and came close to three small herds of elephants, buffaloos and several big flocks of birds, as they all convened on the lake for a dip and drink. The lakeside scenery is very nice. The rest of park appeared in poor status of conservation. Be prepared to join the masses though, in excess of 100 other safari jeeps will be around you!
title: Great, but overcrowded experience

body: We came in the afternoon. at start we didnt see any elephants. Our driver was driving around to find them. Eventually we found a family of around 30 elephants, then we drove somewhere else and so even more. Of course many birds and others. It was fun with many photo opportunities.
title: Elephants - many

body: saw only a handful of elephants, plus a jungle fowl, peacocks and monkeys. It was not the best time of the day if you want to see elephants. We visited between 2 and 4 pm, whereas the best times are either early morning or late afternoon. Anyway, we enjoyed the safari and the views within this famous sanctuary.
title: Wrong Timing!

body: There are parks where you are able to have a much greater sense of adventure, and appreciating it without the masses of tourists one can find here. The number of elephants, however, is spectacular, and definitely worth a visit, if you don't mind competing with another 50 jeeps.
title: Great for seeing wildlife, but a bit overcrowded

body: For me and my family, Minneriya National Park was one of the best vacation experiences ever and for sure the best during our stay in Sri Lanka. The park is simply great and consists all you could want from Elephant Safari. There are dozens or even hundreds of elephants in various siznes, many buffalos and monkeys. You don't event have to be very lucky to have them crossing the road just in the front of you! Summing up, whole jeep safari experience in Minneriya is something that you will remember for a long time :) Recommended!
title: Unique experience, must do in Sri Lanka!!

body: Thousands of elefants and you can stay very close of them. Very nice some elephant babies, and other animals
title: Very nice

body: The elephants come to bathe and drink later in the day, but we saw some elephants amongst the trees earlier in the afternoon. The birds and water buffalo were worth seeing and when the elephants start to move towards the water the excitement really starts. Jeeps are racing to get a good view (everyone gets a good view, its huge!) and standing in the jeep, and hearing the drivers tip each other off all adds to the atmosphere. A fantastic afternoon.
title: Great Jeep Safari to see the elephants

body: Very nice place best to visit around 3.00pm if you want to find lot of animal. This place control by government. Entrance near Gunners pub (Near ali bath kade) is the best place to enter jungle. Best to request one officer to be join your safari vehicle while booking ticket (No extra payment for that). This is a place any one can visit. You must have good quality camera with tripod. Don't forget your hats
title: Only for Nature Lovers

body: We went on this safari at the beginning of July. It was supposed to be one of the best times to see the elephants but luck was not on our side this day. The safari guides suggested it was too hot for them - and it was very hot for us too! We did see some family groups of elephants on the edge of the jungle including some new babies which were very cute. We went on the safari around 2:30 in the afternoon - perhaps later in the day would have been better but that was when we were near the park and our driver said that was the usual time. Later in our trip we visited Udawalawe and that safari was fantastic! The safari took about 3 hours.
title: Baby elephants

body: Had a great time during this safari and we had the chance to see a lot of elephants and some other animals.Highly recommended!
title: Great safari

body: This ranks well ahead of all national parks in Sri Lanka. The reason being the herd of elephants that comes to the water tank.The only issue is the elephants come out in the evening close to the park closing time. We roamed about aimlessly for 2 hours of the 3 hour safari..,looking at buffalos, foxes,monkeys and cows..,when suddenly in the last 30 minutes the elephants come out.The guide/drivers are certain they will come every day except that there is very little time to see them.
title: The best thing you would do in Sri Lanka

body: Yes it is expensive for the jeep and entrance fees - total around 75 dollars for 2 people. Hence the 4 stars. However ! I would totally recommend it ! There were about 100 elephants, you got to see them at different locations in the park. I read about there been loads of other jeeps but actually everyone gets a good view and it doesn't take away from the trip at all. Our driver was great and we were there for around 4 hours. The elephants are so majestic and it's great to see them wild in their own habitat.
title: Worth it!

body: We were lucky - saw lots of elephants, monkeys, buffalo and few birds. Was s little overcrowded but great views and loved the elephants. Part of s prebooked tour - kids loved standing in the jeep
title: Safari

body: We did a jeep safari in the late afternoon as elephants gathered at the water. Mothers, babies and lone male 'tuskers' were encountered along with other wildlife - monkeys, mongooses, a civet and birds of prey, iguanas etc. The elephants were a clear highlight as they gracefully wandered across the plain to the water. There were a lot of jeeps like ours and although we were all a way back from the elephants, I could not help but think we were intruding on their territory and perhaps intimidating/constraining their activities given the number of jeeps
title: Abundant wild elephants and other wildlife

body: If you are after an Elephant Safari, this is the place for you. We counted 51 Elephants of varying ages walk by our jeep to reach the water! Unlike the chaos of Yala National Park, the jeep operators here seem to respect the animals and keep a respectful (safe) distance.Visiting in the evening is best as the animals seek out the cool water at the end of a hot day. an absolute highlight is seeing the little calves no more that a month old frolicking together whilst mums and aunts attempt to corral them in.Green grass, big blue sky, herds of wild elephant and warm tropical breezes, this place says "You are in Sri Lanka".
title: The Gathering

body: We visited Minneriya National Park the first day of our trip in Sri Lanka and it was really unique experience, since we had never seen elephants from that close and in their natural habitat! Our guide, who was really good suggested that we had this safari and it was really worth visiting. We enjoyed the beautiful route inside the park in an open jeep. Except for the elephants the residents of that park are buffaloes and birds. Since anyone visits Sri Lanka I would recommend this activity for sure!
title: Great experience! Recommended!

body: A wonderful few hours which we won't forget. Great for children but make sure they are old enough to sit in an open jeep over rough ground. Our guide told us we had to be there by 2pm to get everything sorted and be in the park by 2.30pm for the arrival of the elephants. He was right and at 2.45pm they started to arrive. We were able to watch different herds arrive, eat and then go for water several times. The proximity was amazing and there were many calves including one of about three weeks. There are also lots of different birds and water buffalo but we went for the elephants!Our local driver was lovely and keen to engage. We saw a lot a trucks turn backless than half way into our trip so unless you want a quick visit take care. Our guide mentioned that some of the companies do that but we saw so much more by going on. Our trip lasted about three hours with lovely spells just stationary watching the elephants.
title: A must see in the area for ekephants

body: This was definitely one of the highlights of our two week stay in Sri Lanka. We were advised by our hotel staff to go late afternoon and thankfully we saw a lot of elephants there at that time. Can't fault this experience, would recommend anyone to go.
title: Great experience

body: Ok, it can get quite crowded by the herd, but it was absolutely magical. We saw loads of elephants, and we were often on our own. Absolutely recommend.
title: Wow!

body: Firstly it has to be said that this was an enjoyable experience; watching elephants in the wild is always an experience. But unfortunately the price just feels extortionate. I would have to echo the other reviews that remark that the amount of other jeeps in the park does somewhat spoil the experience but I guess this is to be expected with any popular tourist destination. Definitely recommend sun cream and sun hat as with the roof off the Jeep you are exposed for quite a prolonged period.
title: A disappointment for the price

body: The ideal place for elephants . there are hundreds of elephants..... Best to visit in afternoons. you should be careful when selecting a Safari Jeep . try to find a 4 wheel as many Indian Jeeps " Maximo" are not 4 wheel . it is not safe to go in a non 4 wheel .
title: Hundreds of Elephants

body: Minneriya national park is a great experience to see large groups of wild elephants. We were recommended to get there early afternoon which i am glad we did. when we got to the large reservoir the elephants were just making their way out of the forest, we got to see around 40 elephants make there way down to the water and then back up to the forest over the space of an hour or so. At this point there were only 3-4 jeeps observing the elephants. I had seen some negative reviews on here about the large hoards of jeeps surrounding the elephants but at this time it was great. On our way back to the main reception area we passed what seemed like 100 jeeps so I feel later in the afternoon would be very crowded and may ruin the experience. We seen online that July was a great time for the elephant gathering but our guide said the colder months were better as the elephants didn't spend so much time sheltering in the Forrest. The trip is not very expensive for a private jeep tour, we spent more on the transfer to get to Minneriya so it is great value for money. Apart from the elephants there are plenty of buffalo, Pelicans, and monkeys.All round fantastic trip but I would be careful about what time of day you visit to avoid teh larger crowds.
title: Amazing experience

body: This park is all about the elephants. However we did see some monkeys, buffaloes, foxes and an eagle. What we remember, though are the beautiful elephants. We probably saw around 100. At first we couldn't find any but suddenly they started coming out of the jungle. We could get really close (few meters)Tours are in the afternoon since this is when elephants come out of the jungle to drink at the "tanks". We left at 3 pm and were back around 6:30 pmWe paid 4500 (30 usd) for the car and then about 25 usd per person for park entrance. Our personal driver arranged it. The tour was 90 usd per person if arranged by our hotel.
title: Elephants

body: Hundreds of elephants wandering around, plus lots of buffalo, eagles, pelicans and monkeys. All of them seem unfazed by the hundreds of jeeps driving people around! Stunningly beautiful park. Loved it.
title: Well worth a trip

body: We were extremely lucky to see two herds of elephants whilst visiting this park this totalled around 100 elephants including males and babies! We also saw a croc, gecko, mongoose, eagle, a variety of monkeys, a kingfisher and herons! We were recommended this park as an ethical alternative to pinnawala which is renowned locally for its mistreatment of elephants including over/ under feeding and chaining them up. I'm glad we made the decision to go here and it was clear that the animals here were wild and in charge of their own environment with plenty of space to roam free. My only criticism of this venue is that some jeep drivers are insensitive to the animals and park in their way to enable tourists to get photographs, resulting in our party witnessing an elephant charge into two vehicles to get them out of the way. Conscious and courteous drivers and tourists are required to maintain the reputation of this park.
title: Amazing, ethical and beautiful

body: We seemed to drive for a very long time along narrow bumpy tracks I wondered if we would even see one elephant, it was not a pleasant drive to start with in the heat and dust but as soon as we drove into the open park area we saw several elephants plenty of bird life and even a crocodile in the distance. We spent a long time driving around different areas of the park seeing a few groups of elephants who came quite close to the jeeps. The drivers are very mindful of the elephants and have nick names for some of them, if they start to get agitated which a few did they backed out the way. One male was injured, limping and bleeding which they reported on our way out nut it was apparently old news. We were told they keep an eye on them all and don't intervene unless absolutely necessary. By the end of the afternoon we mostly stayed in one spot watching them all go down to the water to bathe and keep cool. It was a magical sight seeing the little ones being protected by the older ones. We did not go to any other safari parks as seeing these elephants were enough really. One of the highlights on our Sri Lanka. Tour. Would definitely recommend if you are happy to just see elephants.
title: Elephant families in the wild are a magical sight

body: Our driver did not chase or get too close to any animals, was very respectful and we still saw enough elephants from very close as they got closer while they were busy eating. They totally ignored us, the driver turned off the engine and we were able to really savour the sounds of the elephants eating and a baby elephant playing. A truly special experience for our family.
title: A very special few hours

body: Prepare for a lot of diesel fumes with many ´jeeps together. Elephants are normally at a distance og 50-150 meter away so take a binocular with you. You can be lucky to see elephants, also with baby close up 5-10 meter. Not many other animals can be seen than elephants and birds
title: with some luck a good experiance but animal can be at a distance

body: We took a safari trip on a jeep and were the first jeep to enter the park at 6:30am. We saw herds of elephants ready to return to the jungle. At the lake we saw many different birds....the guide from the park who went along with us explained about wild elephants and different sighting of birds. We appreciated the explaining as we got to know what the animals we saw were like. It was a beautiful day, so we had a wonderful tour. We saw elephants, birds, peacocks, deers.....not a whole lot but we are satisfied. The tour was two hours as it's not a big park. This is near Sigiriya.
title: Saw a family of elephants

body: This place is worth the visit, however i was not aware that i had to pay for the jeep to get inside and the driver entrance fee as well. Also there was service charge of 1600 rupees and a 15% VAT!!! The cost of hiring a jeep was not included with it. In total it cost me 11,420 rupees (4500 rupees for jeep hire) for 2 people (about 55 pounds). Price is cheap but i wasnt aware of the other cost. Other than that, its really worth the visit and i dont regret at all.Next time i made sure i have a hat, sunglasses and scarve, because there was so much dust on me at the end.
title: Suprised with hidden cost!!!

body: We had friends visiting from US and one of the things that they had in their itinerary was to see elephants. While they had read about the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage we convinced them to visit Minneriya National Park instead. They were very thankful for our recommendation as they saw a herd of over 250 elephants in their natural habitat, some bathing, some playing with each other, some tending to their young ones, some grazing, some playing with one another. What more could one expect. The highlight of the trip was when a few elephants decided to to walk back just close past our jeep back to the jungle from the lake. We also saw some peacocks, an eagle and some birds and wild buffalo. Overall a great experience Well worth compared to Pinnawala according to our friends
title: A breathtaking experience with elephants

body: Originally we never had wild life in our itinerary. We had a 2 nights stay in Danawwa resort, as we had plans to to go to Dambulla , sigiriya, trincomalee excursion.Second day after trincomalee, we returned back by noon, we planned to have a jeep safari at 2.30 pm. Local time. It was a hot noon. The entry fee& jeep safari was a costly one. Initially as we entered , thought we may not see anything as it was very hot. But as we passed through thick forest , it was beautiful to see cranes around the lake cooling themselves, few crocodiles,too.Then by around 4 pm, we reached a huge lake & the sight was an unforgettable one. Hundreds of elephants, families &families around the waterbody, were sighted. While coming back, one black langoor, one deer was sighted. On the whole we felt it was worth the money.We reached the main road to Habrana, suddenly one huge single elephant started walking behind our jeep. It was so cute, sincerely it waited to cross the road to enter the forest area. It was awesome. Worth visiting.
title: Keep safari

body: Less jeeps and more animals than Yala. Still alot of jeeps but nothing compared (off season). We saw about 100 elephants and even a 7 day old elephant. Also alot of beautiful birds and other wildlife. Quite an experience.
title: Better than Yala

body: It was a beautiful trip! We hat to wait more than 2 hour but finally the elephants 🐘 came out of the jungle! It was so nice.....
title: Must see

body: Saw around 200 elephants here at the end of June. Highlight of our holiday. Beautiful elephants around the lake, lots of babies, including one only 2 weeks old. There were too many jeeps in the park at once though, we had ticket number 122. Most jeeps keep a good distance from the elephants though, thankfully. Ask your driver to do this. We just had a driver, no guide. Booked through Sanki Leisure for $85 for two adults. Much cheaper than booking through the hotels.
title: Beautiful and emotional visit

body: We hadn't been planning on doing a safari, but eventually we had nothing else to do.We saw around 50 elephants near the main Minneriya tank. Some of the baby elephants were adorable! There was a tusker right kn front of our jeep as well.Besides elephants, there were many birds as well, like herons, pellicans and eagles. Otherwise there was no other wildlife, except two peacocks, two deer and a mongoose. The park itself is very nice to drive around, and has an Africa-like feel to it. There weren't too many jeeps when we went and we didn't see any big crowds. It's best if you can get a jeep with a detachable top so you can stick your head out and take some nice pictures. Our driver was very good, and even cut up a big juicy watermelon for us. I'm not sure if it was fully worth the 40 USD per person, but you won't regret it.
title: Pleasant enough

body: According to the literature, Minneriya National Park has the highest number of elephants per square foot (or hectare or whatever) in Asia. And they weren't kidding. This place has got to be teeming with Asian elephants. The only way into the park is in the back of an open-air jeep and the drivers keep a respectable distance from the elephants. You are still enough to take photos with your iPhone without needing those Nat-Geo super tele zoom lenses. And you will be guaranteed to see the gentle giants in their natural habitat (it's not like they can run off and hide all of a sudden). The only drawback of the park is that it is also teeming with tourists in open-air jeeps. The elephants don't seem to mind and it seems to be supporting a healthy local economy.
title: Elephants, elephants, more elephants, and the occasional water buffalo

body: Great to see lots of herds of elephants and tiny babies with their mums. Very cute. We had a jeep that our driver/guide sorted for us - he knew people... I would highly recommend this if you love wildlife or have never been on a safari before. Although it was mainly elephants, there were birds and even golden eagles flying around. Our driver tried to leave after 1 hour but we persisted on staying as they said it would last 2/3 hours in total. After that hour we got even closer to the elephants!! I would also recommend you guiding the driver to the spots you want to go to if the jeeps are permitted to do so.
title: Elephant extravaganza

body: Elephants galore and up close.We decided we didn't want to go to the commercial elephant orphanages as we didn't want to see elephants in chains. We were so pleased we came here.
title: Great park

body: We saw about 5 herds of elephants, about 40 in all. It seems the numbers can cross 100 at times. The best was see the little ones, especially in the water and getting a mud bath.
title: Great place to see and enjoy elephants

body: This was a good safari and saw many elephants and our driver and guide knew where they were and which males not to get too close to. Some didn't and got chased for being too cheeky. We still got close and saw little baby elephants with there mums which was very sweet. Worth the rough ride in and would recommend.
title: Many elephants

body: If you want to see wild elephants you should really visit this national park. We saw over more then a hundred elephants, male, females, new borns all kinds of ages and two different kinds of elephants. Water buffalos, lots of special birds and monkey's you can spot here as well. We went in the low season but there were a lot of cars, can't imagine how this will be in the high season, I would recommend to go in low season.
title: Lot's of elephants!

body: Such a good experience!We came to see the Elephants and boy did we see them, there must have been over 100. There were a few very young babies too which was a great bonus.We saw monkeys, lizards, buffalo, parakeets, peacocks and loads of other birds. We heard there is a leopard family but I think they are pretty elusive and our guide didn't really bother looking.We went about 16:00 which seemed to be a popular time.
title: Elephants Elephants Elephants!

body: If your intention is to see a lot of elephants, this will be exactly what you are getting. We saw packs of 50 elephants together, from all sizes, roaming freely. Some elephants came up to 2 meters of the jeeps. Amazing experience!!Do not expect to see a lot of other mammals like in for instance Yala. Other downside is you will definitely not be alone. Even though we visited in off season, everywhere you will be accompanied by other jeeps. Some good birdlife as well!
title: All about the elephants

body: We visited the park with a driver and guide, arranged through our accommodation in Habarana. The visit was great, seeing about a 100 elephants. We visited the park in the afternoon as the elephants walk to the lake, in their own time, to drink. Late in the afternoon, there were (too) many jeeps, some of which ended up blocking the elephants path to the lake.This was quite disturbing to see and something for the park watch to take on.
title: Worth a visit in season

body: Our hotel in Polonnaruwa arranged Safari for us amazing day and saw at least100 elephants during our trip. There were many jeeps but each jeep had their moment to view elephants. We loved it. Book locally and you get best price.
title: Great Safari

body: Lovely park. Jeep safari excellent- saw around 200 elephants gathered, a truly wonderful sight. They looked happy and whilst not too bothered by the jeeps were wild and charged if we got too close! Much better way to see these wonderful animals than in captivity
title: Elephants

body: This safari is a must for anyone interested in watching herds of elephants in their natural habitat, slow march to their "waterhole." The Jeeps get you fairly close to these beasts of the jungle, who allow you to watch them if you respect their space.
title: The majestic walk of the wild elephants

body: Minneriya is in North central of Sri Lanka. Went on a Jeep Safari in the afternoon where it was advice to go at that time to see a large herd of elephant on the banks of the minneriya tank. Managed to see more than 100 elephants at the sight.
title: Place to See a Large Herd of Wild Elephants

body: During the first twenty minutes in the jeep we thought that we were being taken for a ride. Then we saw an elephant and took a series of fotos. And then we drove on for a while and all of a sudden the track opened up and we saw them: more than 150 elephants! And in what landscape! A beautiful lake and flocks of interesting birds like ostriches, pelicans, cormorans ... It was amazing how close you could get to the elephants. And there were so many baby elephants! It was the experience of a lifetime, just great!
title: A unique experience

body: Very nice experience of seeing wild animals, we saw especially lots of elephants. It cost has 80$ for a couple, a four hour trip in a privet jeep. Totally worth thr money, the view is unforgettable.
title: minneriya national park

body: we went around 2. pm to national park. first we take look of the museum, at that time more than 50 jeeps were check in to the park. really cool. had a great wild experience with my friend and the jeep driver show us more than 200 elephants. nice place to visit in sigiriya. hope to come again back as soon as possible
title: amazing safari

body: Minneriya is a great safari if you want to see elephants because you will see tons and tons of them. We actually got very close to them as they did not seem to mind the jeeps! However not much other wildlife, some birds by the lake and a fox and that was it. There were a lot of other safari groups at the same time and be aware that you will get quite dusty. Also entrance fee is nearly 4000 rupees but most attractions are similarly quite expensive.
title: Lots and lots of elephants!

body: We had a great time at the Minneriya park with my family, saw many elephants, birds, wildboar, deer and in fact one of the Elephant started charging at us coz he thought we were way too close to his comfort zone. it was.
title: A Wild Experience

body: We went here on a private jeep tour, organised by our host at Habarana Wild Resort, Indika. The journey from Habarana was interesting and very safe and comfortable.At Minneriya we picked up a local ranger who was our guide - and he was invaluable for his knowledge and 'spotting' ability - pointing out birds and wildlife that we may have missed without him.And the wildlife - we saw a jackal, crocodile, water buffalo, eagles, monkeys, a bear monkey - oh and elephants! The first group was of about a dozen, which we were amazed at - then we drove on and there were more, and another group, and another - possibly 70 wild, free elephants of all ages, sizes and temperament - marvellous.This is the ultimate way to see elephants in their natural habitat and we wouldn't have missed it for the world.
title: Elephants, elephants, elephants!

body: A splendid place to "Shake hands with the Elephants" also some beautiful birds in their natural habitat. A must see place.
title: MARVELLOUS PLACE
